utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar, today is 7 July 2010. I would like first of all to great the witness, whom I can see on the screen, Mr. Marcussen, Ms. Biersay, as well as their associates. I would like to greet Mr. Seselj and all those helping us in this courtroom. For a few minutes I would like to talk to the witness who is in Belgrade to tell him after what he had thought he heard yesterday, i.e., that an interpreter had mentioned "scums" Seselj's men, the Registry checked the audio recording and did not acknowledge that the term "scum" had been mentioned or translated from B/C/S. Witness, you may have misunderstood, which might explain why you mentioned this. Actually, yesterday when you were telling us about this, I was looking at Mr. Seselj very closely to try and understand whether he had heard that as well. Mr. Seselj would have undoubtedly raised an objection. Since he wasn't saying anything, I concluded in the meantime that he may not have heard that since he was busy doing other things, or maybe he hadn't heard it at all. So I have been told that the audio recording has been officially checked and that you have mentioned is not on it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I couldn't believe my own ears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished. I would like to add that the interpreters are working in very difficult conditions. These are professionals who have been doing their job for a great number of years. There might be a mistake in the translation from time to time. That can happen to anyone. In this case it would have been a serious matter had it been the case. The material evidence, of course, is audio recording, which we have. Witness, do you have anything to say, a comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard, or perhaps -- well, I can't say for sure. Perhaps it was a similar word, and since my hearing is impaired 45 per cent on both ears, it is possible that I heard wrong, but I didn't react vehemently. I just mentioned the fact and said that it was impermissible to speak like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, I didn't. I just made a bit of a joke when you mentioned my name, I said I might have heard it, but I couldn't believe my own ears. That was just a pleasantry. I didn't hear anything, that's true, but I do have a lot of criticisms with respect to the work of the interpretation service, and I've already said that before. But no, I really didn't hear that word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So thank you very much. This matter has been settled. Mr. Marcussen, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, yesterday you testified the following: "I was brought an invitation without a signature requesting me to attend an interview in such and such a place at such, at such a time." That is for Your Honours' reference, page 16185, lines 3 and 4. Mr. Jovic, when was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that was -- let me see. I don't know the exact date, but to the best of my recollections, if that means anything to you, when the Croatian embassy was stoned after some water polo match, although you don't know about that, but anyway, that's a rough estimate of the time. I can't give you an exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you give us a year?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did receive it. 1993. 2003. I apologise. 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who brought you the invitation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two men who didn't introduce themselves or show any ID cards. It was difficult to reach my house because the road was being reconstructed, so they parked 200 metres away, and they came by as I described it, and they handed me this invitation without a signature or stamp, just with the Tribunal letterhead in the upper right-hand corner or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where were you supposed to go? It was an invitation to go where?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the office of The Hague Tribunal in Jevremova Street, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When? How long after you received the invitation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- I really can't remember. I don't know. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was it -- was it within in a month of the invitation, two months, half a year, a year? What? How long?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I just can't remember. It might have been a shorter period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How did you get from your home to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By bus, the morning coach, which starts out at 3.30 from Mali Zvornik, 3.30 a.m., and arrives in Belgrade early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you travel alone or was someone with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the bus was full of workers, but I was on my own. As far as my family's concerned, they stayed at home. But that's where the bus stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And from the bus station in Sarajevo, how did you -- I'm sorry, from the bus-stop where you got off in Belgrade to the field office, how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know Belgrade very well. I worked in Montenegro for a long time, and Sarajevo, and those parts. I know them better. So I went -- well, I lost my way, and I was walking past an embassy that had been destroyed and asked a policeman there, and he said that it was in the Dedinje area by the Dragisa Miscevic Hospital, and that's how I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you came to the field office, who did you meet with?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met with the interpreter and the lady investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they know that you were coming? Had you called to say what day you would come, or how had that come about, or did they not expect you to arrive --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, they knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How did they know?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume they knew. When I rang the bell at the entrance at the gate, not me but the policeman, they came to get me. They came down the stairs to the front entrance to collect me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And now that we have talked a bit more about the details, maybe your memory has come back as to when this might have been.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been June, July. The weather was nice. I was just wearing a T-shirt and sandals, so it must have been June or July sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Of 2002 or of 2003, or what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So it was quite a long time after you had received the invitation that you actually came to the field office?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not receiving any interpretation, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you had received the invitation to tell you to come to the field office in 2002, so you received the invitation at least half a year before you actually went to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I mention 2002 anywhere? Who said 2002?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just a minute ago when I asked you about it, when this might have taken place. But let's -- let's move to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, unless I'm mistaken, at line 23, page 5, he said 2003.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what I said, but there we go. You can have a look and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I apologise if I have mixed up the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I can refer you to something else you testified about yesterday, and I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, the Judges do not understand fully why you are putting all these questions. You must have your own reasons. You have something like 40 minutes left, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I think I had 50 minutes left when I started, so that might be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about some other things you testified about yesterday. And for Your Honours' reference, I'm referring to page 16177. Mr. Jovic, you testified yesterday that you were threatened, blackmailed, and a number of other things. I'd like to talk a bit about that. You said that your family was threatened. When was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- just a moment. Let me try and remember. 2000 and -- and -- and well I'm not very good with dates, to be honest, but bear with me. It was after I had given my statement to the Defence team and when I -- when I clashed with Janko Lakic, and that was in 2003, the end of June perhaps. Janko Lakic. Please don't hold it against me. I just can't remember. I'm a sick man. My centre for equilibrium has been affected. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But -- so it was -- you described the incident, I believe, yesterday about Janko Lakic. So it was after you had given your statements to the OTP. You said -- you also testified that you were threatened with prison. When was that threat made?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who threatened me with prison? You mentioned Janko Lakic, and then you went on to ask about threatening with prison. He didn't threaten me, it was Rita Pradham that threatened me with the central prison in Belgrade that I would be taken to The Hague, to prison there and that I would sing like a canary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then she said we'll see what you're going to do to you -- you'll see what we're doing to do to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the office up above, on the floor above.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 2003. That's when the threats started. But they weren't uttered every day -- on one day. Every day was dramatic and different. When I signed my statement, for instance. It was mostly on that date, and I pushed the statement to her side of the table. She pushed it back. I didn't want to sign it. So I'd like to ask the Honourable Judges to confront this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You -- you said that you would -- that at -- a statement had been written up for you. When were you shown -- were you shown a statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the table. When? When I was supposed to sign it, on that day. I can't give you an exact date. I can't remember. It was in 2003, perhaps -- well, I don't know. I'm really not good with dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. So -- but you're saying that this was at the time that you were asked to sign your statement in 2003; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I don't know whether it was 2003. Yes, it was. And -- and -- and -- well, I don't know. There's no point. I just can't remember the date. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You also said that you had been blackmailed. What were you blackmailed with?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, don't misunderstand me. I don't want to have any trouble with you, but would this be a threat to you: "Sign or else." And think of your family. Think of your children. What could -- what could I deduce from that? I was in Belgrade. My children were in Mali Zvornik. What would happen to them? So that's how they threatened me, with an indictment for Zvornik as well. Now, you have a computer in your head and you don't want to ask, but some policemen have already given their statements, and you could tell us the truth, that people -- that you killed people in Drinjaca. Then in Drinjaca they would take you to court. But I said that I would cut off my own right hand if anybody touched my children.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said. The interpreter didn't understand him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It lasted 14 hours. The interview lasted 14 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was that -- was that the interview when you signed your statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was when I signed the statement. There were threats then, and there were threats before if I didn't want to co-operate, if I didn't want to talk, if I didn't want to be a witness against Vojislav Seselj, not only him but against others too. Franko Simatovic, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who made those threats?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Rita Pradham. I don't know how you pronounce her name, that H in the middle of her surname, but anyway, Pradham. I assume you know who that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you say she repeated these threats to you later. When was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that she would dose out her threats every time I went in for an interview. Sometimes they went on for four days, if I remember correctly. So when I came for the interview, there would always be something when I stopped talking and didn't want to say what didn't happened, she would say, Well, either you're going to say it or you're going to -- well, you can walk out freely, but I'll tell your MUP to arrest you and take you to the central prison and then you'll have to wait there for me to come and get you out and you have to pray to God that I come soon, who knows when I come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So every time you met with the investigator that is what she told you or similar things. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not straight away. There would be a nice story first of all, all wrapped up in foil, but then when she got to the nitty-gritty and wanted to make me own up and say that the police had killed in Drinjaca some 100 Muslims, that's when it started. And I didn't want to. I know that that didn't happen. I would have heard about it if it had, from my colleagues. And when I didn't want to own up to that and say that the police did that because I know it never did then the threats would start and she would say, If you don't say it then we'll raise an indictment against you for such and such. I didn't know that she couldn't do that that you couldn't raise indictments any more, and whether she had the right to raise the indictment without instructions from the Tribunal, I didn't know any of that. All I did was attend a policeman's course so I'm not well versed in other matters of law. I'm not an educated policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you were --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me to be able to defend myself with those allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a follow-up question. I have listened to Mr. Marcussen's questions as well as your answers and you have said that you are a policeman and you know how all this works. So more than anyone you know that police, sometimes, when conducting investigations, use this kind of method and say to someone, It's in your best interest to talk about things. The Judges will bear this in mind. Think of your family, and so on. Very often this is how things happen, and this didn't mean necessarily that it is blackmail. What do you have to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I say is this: I didn't say that I was just a policeman for me to know the system according to which the police worked. All I said was that I attended a short training course and that I was no match for an investigator who studied things like that. That's what I just said, if that's what you're referring to, what I just said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Witness, I'd like you to tell me, please, the following: This so-called blackmail purportedly led you to giving false statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. And everybody would do the same if their family and children's lives were at stake. When it comes to your home and children and their life, everybody would behave like that, any normal man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that you gave false statements to save your children's lives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I said what Janko Lakic dictated in order to save my family from misery, poverty. And they threatened to kill me too. They threatened to beat me to death, not to kill me with firearms. So with a should I have done? I had an underaged child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Perhaps there's something I've misunderstood. Who was actually threatening you? You mentioned somebody's name. I haven't quite understood who it was. I need to check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you started asking me who threatened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was Janko Lakic who supposedly threatened you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to give a false statement that the Seselj Defence team maltreated us in the offices of the Serbian Radical Party. I thought you were asking me about that. If not, if we're talking about Rita, we can move on to that subject then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought maybe I'm mistaken, but I thought that on the basis of the questions put to you by the Prosecutor, you were answering about blackmail that would have been done by the OTP. Maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can talk about that, too, but I thought you asked me about who blackmailed me in order to give a false statement. I think that is how you phrased your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's set aside what we've been talking about. I'll check that later. Now, I'd like to know the following: When you were interviewed by the member -- members of the OTP, you were intimidated --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Interviewed me in 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes. And then was there blackmail at that moment? Were you intimidated? Was any pressure exerted against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There was intimidation, blackmail, threats were made, pressure was put upon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will answer to the Prosecutor regarding this matter, but I have very specific detail to get from you. In 2003, you made false statements. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2003, I gave a statement, but a statement was drafted for me. I was given a statement that I was to learn by heart. It was this thick, more or less, and then I was told --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does not reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rita drafted it, so it didn't correspond to anything. I was to learn it by heart. Why would I have to learn something that is true by heart? If you ask me a question, in ten years' time I will repeat what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So just so we understand your last answer to the Judge correctly, what you're saying is that you were put under pressure to give false information, to sign a statement which is not true. That's what you're saying, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I was put under pressure to admit something that I didn't do and something that I didn't see. There were threats, there was blackmail. Bribes were offered and so on and so forth. The statement isn't false, but some of her arguments, some of her philosophical thoughts, were inserted in the statement, but I can say this is what I said and this is what Rita said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I wanted to come to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when was it that you were offered to stay in a hotel with girls for six months at the Tribunal's expense?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Rita Pradham said that I would have six months in a hotel. She said I would stay in a hotel for six months in Holland. I would be surrounded by beautiful women. But there was this Predrag Momcilovic, I really don't know his exact surname, who was a member of her team and he added, "You'll be able to avail yourself of their services at the expense of the Tribunal," and Rita added that she would take me to court to see how witnesses testify against Seselj fared so I could get over my nervousness because he --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My question is: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you quite clearly. This wasn't told to me on one sole occasion. Such offers were made when I had to sign this very lengthy statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So it was said during the time that your statements were prepared. So that means it was said at the time when the investigator, language assistants, and other people were present; right? You say this was during the interview itself.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Predrag who was present and Jasmina, the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Right. The front page of your statements record all those who were present. Thanks for that. Now I'd like to move to something else. Let me just say one thing to you or ask you about something. Yesterday you testified in response to Judge Lattanzi. You said, and this is at page 16214, at the bottom and following on the next page: "Madam Judge, let me just explain something to you. The interpretation I received was -- I received was 'How were you forced? How did they force you?' That is why, with all due respect, I have to say, and I apologise for that, but nobody can force me to do anything." Yet you are telling us that you as a trained policeman --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My question's coming now. So nobody -- you're somebody who cannot be forced to do anything, yet you say that the Prosecution forced you to sign statements which are false. That's what you're telling the Court today, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait for my answer. Wait for my answer, please. I want the truth to come out. When my children are at stake, when my family is at stake --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That was not my question.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the lives of my children are at stake then I am at my most vulnerable. Well, I want the truth to be known. That's the truth. I can't tell you what you want to hear. I can only tell you how things actually were. And that's the truth. No one can deny that. I'm saying this under oath. I can take the solemn declaration again. I can do that every morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's one thing I don't understand, Witness. You said that Mr. Lakic threatened you, that you were afraid for your lives, you were afraid for your family, and you mentioned other reasons for blackmail, the hotel, the beautiful women, so forth and so on. That's when it comes to the members of the OTP. So please don't confuse the issue. We have two situations, and don't mix them up. So what exactly is -- what exactly does your family have to do with this other kind of blackmail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. At an interview in Belgrade -- well, I spent four days in Belgrade giving an interview. She said, Think about your family, about your children. How do I know who's in my house at the time? I couldn't trust her. I couldn't believe anything she said. She had power. I didn't. I didn't have a lawyer. I wasn't allowed anything. I didn't even know how to ask for certain things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the members of the OTP mentioned your own family and your own children. Are you absolutely sure? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, this morning I asked you the same question and you told me that it was Lakic who had threatened you. When did anybody from the OTP threaten your family?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a minute. All these questions will probably be dealt with by another person who will be in charge of investigating these allegations. However, the Prosecutor is entitled to put questions to you to check your credibility, but just one detail in passing. You're talking about your children, and of course everyone's interested. I'm looking at the document. You were married in 1983, and a child was born in 1984. In 2003, this child is 19 years old. It's not a baby. It's no longer a baby. So why are you so worried about a 19-year-old? It's an adult.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a son who was born in 1998. How old was he at the time? I had this son with my second wife. My first wife died. His name is Radomir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But in your statement in 2003, you don't mention this second son of yours, and you even mention your second marriage. Very well. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, when did anybody from OTP threaten your family?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, isn't it a threat when you say, Admit that you killed that person in Drinjaca, think about your children. What was I to think? If I didn't say certain things, someone would go and take my child away or do something to my family. I live in a forest. My house is surrounded by a forest. I have no neighbours there. My wife is alone with the children. On one occasion for that reason I fled. I didn't want to remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ran home. In the morning they phoned me, called me, and asked me, What are you doing at home?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, isn't it true that actually you voluntarily came to the Belgrade field office and proposed to be considered as a potential witness?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true that I went there voluntarily. I received a summons, and then I went then. Naturally it's not that I had to, but it wasn't really of my own accord. How should I put it? I received a summons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, I have one small question for you. There might be an error in the transcript. You say this morning I put the same question to you. Have you met this witness? Did you meet the witness this morning? Did you say this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I might have said this morning. That is due to -- what I meant was it was my first questions during the session. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm reassured. Thank you. It would have been a time-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And actually when you came to the field office you brought with you 26 documents that you handed over to the investigator at the Office of the Prosecutor, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first occasion I wasn't asked to do that, but on the second occasion I was asked to bring all the documents I had. I brought everything I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my wartime experience in Darda and elsewhere, Tenja.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you came to the field office, you said you were prepared to be a witness but that you needed protective measures.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They offered me protective measures of their own accord. I asked them why I needed protective measures, why should I need a glass partition. Then they mentioned a third country, and I spoke to the VWU and filled in a form of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VWU is a very decent department, one of the most decent ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I certainly agree with that. The first investigator you met at the field office, that was not the investigator Rita, was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator was Rita.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, after you had met, you had went to the Office of the Prosecutor in -- on the 17th of June, 2003. You went back, and on the 10th, 11th, 14th and 15th of July, 2003, you were interviewed by a number of members of the Office of the Prosecutor; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They took turns when interviewing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And it was different interviewers during the different days.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the first day you met Rita, but the next day she wasn't there, was she?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Rita was always present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I went to a room. May I finish my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No. You have answered. You say she was always present. And then a statement was drawn up, but it was not signed. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I can't remember, but I'm not saying that that wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And for Your Honours' reference, that statement that was drawn up is in Your Honours' binder number 2, the one called "Notice of compliance with Trial Chamber order 8 December 2009," and it's under tab number 2. The 65 ter number is 04626479, 04626500.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then in -- on the 28th of September, 2003, you went back to the field office again, and there you actually signed the statement that --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- had been prepared in July.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in what way did I sign this? I told you how this came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, but what I'm saying is you went back to the Office of the Prosecutor in September, on the 28th of 2003, and you signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again without summons. Did I appear there without having been summoned? You're claiming that on the first occasion I went there without having been summoned? Is that what you're saying, that I hadn't been summoned? Try and be a lit bit more courteous. You're doing your work very well, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a technical question, and I'm sure that the person who will be in charge of investigates will probably put this question to you also. When you signed this document that I have, a document that is 24 pages long, you signed it on September 28, 2003. We have the date. I would like to know whether the -- before you signed the document, the interpreter actually read over the entire statement in your own language, all paragraphs of this statement, the 142 statements in this -- 142 paragraphs in the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Read it out from a laptop, read out the statement while it was being drafted, and later they brought me the statement so that I could sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is important. When you signed the statement, the interpreter read over the 142 paragraphs in your own language and you signed after having heard all these paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter didn't read anything out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I wanted to know. They didn't read anything out. They just gave you the document and asked you to sign all the pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the interpreter will probably be interviewed by the investigator. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the statement we have just been discussing has 65 ter number 07327.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In October 2005, you contacted the Office of the Prosecutor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never contacted them. They would always contact me. They had my phone number at home, and they would phone me when it was necessary for me to appear then tell me when to come, but in October, Rita issued a wanted notice for me because I was in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: On the -- on the 24th of October, 2005, you called the Office of the Prosecutor. You actually spoke to Rita, and you reported security concerns, and the next day one of her colleagues spoke to you about the concerns, didn't he? So you called because you were afraid you'd been at a conference. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the reason I phoned. You're right, I remember that now. You are quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you did call the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I phoned her quite simply because -- just a minute. Let me complete my answer. I have to explain this. It's the truth. I want to tell you the truth. It's not that simple. You can't just say, I phoned them and that's it. This is an act of aggression against a witness who is trying to tell you the truth. Would you allow me to explain to you the reason for which I phoned them. If not, say so and that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My question was whether you had contacted the Office of the Prosecutor. You had. You spoke to Rita, you confirmed that you had called her. Now, you reported -- you called because you were concerned about your security. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, we have a document which is -- has 65 ter number 07329, which is in the binder that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the security concern that you had, that you called Rita about?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't worried about my own safety. I tried to find out where the protection I was being offered actually was, and on another occasion I said my best friend was threatening me. What did they do about that? Nothing. Nobody did anything. Then I saw that they were just telling me lies. It was just a matter of deception. I was supposed to put my head in a bag, go abroad and live on the street there, beg. That's what Rita promised me. That's why I phoned her to, see what sort of possibilities she had. Your Honours, do you understood me? I phoned her but she wanted to take my family into the unknown. I wanted to see whether everything that was said was true, but I realised it was just a matter of deception. I -- I'm quite sure that you're not involved in this, but it was Rita.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then you were contacted again by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 13th of October, 2006, and you were asked to meet with the Office of the Prosecutor again with a view to take a statement. And you did actually meet with the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you are under oath. You took an oath, and you said that you would tell the truth, and you said that you want to say everything and say the truth, which is why you are testifying opening, and I congratulate you on being frank, but in our file we have a declaration made by you on October 21st of 2005 to the OTP -- on the 25th of October, 2005, in the OTP, you say that you're a radio ham, et cetera, et cetera, that you heard a number of information, various things, that you heard a person called Zlatko Peric talking over the radio about atrocities that had happened in Zvornik during the war, and you were afraid, afraid that you could be destroyed as a Prosecution witness. This is what you said in this statement. Have you forgotten everything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. I forgot about that. You're right. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who were you afraid of at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was only afraid of going abroad. I was afraid of how I would be received there. I was worried about whether I would have appropriate living conditions there, about whether I'd be able to feed my children. Perhaps it would no longer be possible to return. So that's why I wanted to check out the possibilities that Rita had. Or sometimes I tried to check things with Christine Dalj. I said Novak Savic is threatening me. He's my best friend. He has diabetes, he's 70 plus year old. She said, Do you have a passport? I said, Yes. She said, The VWU from Sarajevo will contact you. Then Mr. Mike, I respect him, well, he carries out the Tribunal's orders. Well, I don't really know what those Tribunal structure's like. Please let me complete my answer. Be patient. This was on Thursday, and he said, Next week I won't be here. When I return, we'll deal with the matter. So what would have happened if Novak Savic had really threatened me? By the time Mike appeared next week, I would have spent seven days in my grave. Then I saw that this was all just a matter of deception and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a professional person like myself reading this statement can draw the following conclusion, but I'm talking under your control because you said all this to the Prosecutor. You heard on the radio, on the radio ham, a person called Peric talking about what might have happened in Zvornik. You say that this Peric was -- that this Peric was a member of a paramilitary group, that you might be blamed for the atrocities that happened in Zvornik, and that's when you become so frightened. You say that you're frightened that families will want to take revenge on you. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that Peric -- well, this -- a Muslim friend of mine told me about this from Zvornik, that Zlatko Peric, and Zlatko Peric is one of our radio hams, and he said that they were -- they had a party with the Muslims, and he said that I had committed evil deeds around Zvornik and that I was frightened of revenge, people taking revenge on me, Muslims. But they're my neighbours. They come to my house now because I didn't do any of that, of course. So Zlatko and I forgot about that later on. We were able to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you also tell the Prosecutor, "I was waiting for the right moment to tell you this?" Did you also tell the Prosecutor that you were afraid of the radicals or members of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't say that I was afraid of the Serbian Radical Party. What I said was somebody might kill me who lost their family in the war, an ordinary man who didn't belong to any party, because I live in the border belt where people were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of this is extremely complex. A professional investigator and a very experienced person is the only person who can look into all of this. This may take a lot of time. The Judges do not have the material capability to deal with all of this. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You met again with Rita, a lawyer, and interpreters on the 18th and 19th of October, 2006, and that's when you signed the statement that we talked about yesterday. We already went over that yesterday. Now, then you called Rita again on the 9th of January, 2007, and the reason you called was that you had been contacted by the accused's Defence team. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't call Rita -- what date did you say, the 19th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The 9th of January, the 9th of January, 2007. You called because you had been contacted by the Defence team who wanted to speak to you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 19th of January, 2007, I was -- I might have called Christine Dahl. Might that not be a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She called me a number of times, and I called --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We will get to this in a minute, I believe. You called Rita. You told that the Defence team wanted to speak to you, and what you were told was that you could speak to them and that you should tell the truth. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't call Rita. I don't remember calling Rita, and I do believe that I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just -- okay. Then in September -- on the 5th of September, 2007, you were contacted by the Office of the Prosecutor who wanted to meet you, and you agreed to meet representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Since they called me, I had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you met with them on the 21st of September, 2007, and that's when you told them about the statements that you had given to the Defence team of the accused in January 2007. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Probably it was like that. Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you brought with you -- you spoke about a number of documents, and on the 1st of October you met with some people at the field office and there was a video-conference and you signed a statement about what you said were threats and falsification of the statements you had given in January. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I explained why --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I know what you said. I just wanted to be clear that we agree that you did give a statement on the 1st of October. And when you met with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 1st of October, you came with a number of documents. You brought a statement dated the 29th of January, 2007, which is your Defence statement which had been certified before the Belgrade court -- one of the courts in Belgrade. You also brought a letter that you had written to the accused, and you brought a statement that you had made yourself retracting the 29th January 2007 statement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, while we're waiting to be connected again, I could raise two issues, administrative ones, and so that we just have one left for the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I think all of a sudden he's there on the screen again. We shall keep these housekeeping matters for the end of the hearing. Mr. Marcussen, our witness is back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, do you remember my question?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you came on the 1st of October to the field office, you brought three documents with you. You brought a copy of one of the versions of the statement you had given to the Defence, dated the 29th of January, 2007. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you also brought with you a letter, a handwritten letter, that you told the Prosecution you had sent to the accused, Mr. Seselj. Is that true? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you brought a statement that you had gone to have certified yourself in which you retract your 29 January statement. Isn't that true? You gave that to the Office of the Prosecutor that day.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 20th of January? I can't remember the date, but I did bring them that, and I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents in question are 65 ter numbers 07331, 07332, 07334, and 07335. In light of time I can't show these documents to the witness, but I also believe in light of his answers there's no dispute that these documents were given. He already talked about this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, then after this --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I going to have a chance to explain why I brought them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you going to give me the opportunity of explaining why I brought those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's just go through my questions. On the 16th of November, 2007, you contacted a member of the Victims and Witnesses Unit because you wanted to get in touch with the Office of the Prosecutor, and you wanted the Office of the Prosecutor to know that you were afraid because --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was invited to go to the premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you contacted -- well, actually let's --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Can you hear me now? Is it better?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hear you now. I can hear you very well, but I can't hear the interpreter. Yes, I've just heard him. I can hear the interpreter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Actually, let me go back just a little bit, just a few days back. On the 5th of November, 2007, you contacted a member of the Victims and Witnesses Unit because you wanted to speak to the OTP, to the Office of the Prosecutor, and you wanted to clarify some details about when you had had a visa for Russia issued. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come the Victims and Witnesses Unit sent it to Russia and that I knew the telephone number? I contacted Christine Dahl concerning all these questions of migration and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you also wanted to give another statement to the Office of the Prosecutor because there was another version of the statement that you had signed on the 29th of January, 2007, to the Defence team. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Because isn't it a fact, as you explain in your letter to Seselj, that you initially gave a statement to the Defence team on the 29th of January, which was recorded by the Defence team? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean? I don't understand. Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: On the 29th of January, 2007, when you gave your statements to the Defence team, the Defence team record -- had a tape recorder and recorded part of your -- of what you said.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then they drafted up a statement for you to sign.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You weren't really given a proper opportunity to read it through, and you were taken off to the 4th District Court where your signature was certified. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so you had a signed statement now given to the Defence, but then you read through the statement and you weren't satisfied with it, and you complained to members of the accused's Defence team about the statement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was satisfied with my statement, but under pressure from Janko Lakic, and I described those pressures, from Janko Lakic, and that's how the statement came to be brought, within that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, because the truth is, as you explained in your letter to the accused, that because you were not satisfied with the statement, another version of the statement was drafted up. Isn't that true? So your first statement that was signed on the 21st of -- or drafted on the 29th of January, 2007, was certified on the 31st of January, 2007; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But then you make another -- but then you --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then there is another version of the same statement which is a new version of the statement, and that is actually certified in March. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And that is because you were not happy with the first version of the statement, so you went back and another version was made of the statement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was because it was recorded on a Dictaphone and needed to be retyped, and when it was retyped, I was called to court to certify it. I read it and it was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then some time passed and you received a call from Lakic, who also had given a statement, who realised that things had been inserted into the statement. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been true for him, but mine was correct, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you went to the office -- when the Office of the Prosecutor contacted you, you explained in detail what parts of the statement were incorrect and in what way, which parts were not true, which parts were partially true, and that's what you explained in detail to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 1st of October, 2007. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to talk because of the threats. So I had to say it the way they told me to. And the young woman sitting next to me, she -- she circled some paragraphs more than me, and I had to behave properly just so that I could get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that I was between suicide and coming here. That was the situation. A rock and a hard place. You don't understand all the problems you've inflicted upon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so you're claiming that Lakic threatened you and then somebody from the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Marcussen. Your time is up. Please try to conclude now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you're claiming that Lakic threatened you and then the Office of the Prosecutor manipulated your hand to encircle a number of parts in your statement. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the statement that you mentioned and said where we circled the paragraphs, what I said, what Verice Radeta said. Is that the statement you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is the statement I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said -- so it's that one. And that's what I had -- why I had to do what I knew would be -- that you would be satisfied with it, because goodness knows what I would have experienced otherwise. I was afraid of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Isn't it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not you. I don't mean you personally. I mean the investigators. I don't blame or accuse the Judges or you. To be quite frank, I respect you, and I apologise for my temperament and for raising my voice, but those people who threatened me and made problems for me, when I came there I was afraid of them. When I -- when I came here, I was afraid of them. But otherwise, everybody was nice to me and deserve every respect, and I can say that publicly so that the whole world can hear, as far as my treatment here today and yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And isn't it true --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But before that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Isn't it true that then -- isn't it true that in November when it became known in the public that you were going to be a witness in this case, you became very worried, and then you retracted the statement you had given on the 1st of October because you were afraid of the consequences of being a witness here? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent a statement before that to the Defence team, before November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You retracted your statement that you gave to the Defence team in a statement to the OTP, and then you retracted the statement you had given to the OTP retracting your Defence team's statement because you were afraid when it became known you were a witness. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true about November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And isn't it true --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, investigator Rita Pradham never threatened you, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Witness. Let Mr. Marcussen put --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am on oath here, and I will take the oath again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are under oath. As Mr. Marcussen is going to finish putting his questions to you, listen carefully to what he tells you and then you may state your position, but you are overlapping all the time and it is difficult to follow. I would like to listen carefully to what Mr. Marcussen is saying and then listen carefully to what you have to say. Mr. Marcussen, start again, because there has been a lot of overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, I'm putting to you that you are not telling the truth when you are alleging that investigator Rita Pradham, of the Office of the Prosecutor, ever threatened you. That is not true, is it, Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can take the oath again on pain of being criminally prosecuted and on my moral responsibility that everything is as I have told it. It's the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as far as the threats are concerned from Rita Pradham, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And it is not true --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have taken the solemn declaration here so I am speaking on oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you said. What are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And it is not true that a person called Predrag from the Office of the Prosecutor promised you dancing girls at a hotel in The Hague for six months. That is just not true, is it, Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I said -- I said for the first question it's true. It's not that it's not true. It's true that Rita threatened me and (redacted), or whatever, said that I would have dancing girls and could use their services at the expense of the Tribunal. So I can take the solemn declaration again and I swear on my child, the child that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling the truth here, sir, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, you want this Court to believe that Rita Pradham who had threatened you is the very person you called on two occasions when you felt threatened. That is the person you called and reached out to. You really want this Court to believe that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I wanted to check out her capabilities, whether she could and would protect me or not, but she didn't have the possibility to do that. She couldn't protect herself, let alone me, and she threw me into this abyss, and as I'm still on oath, I can swear that that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you did call here because you wanted protection. Now, I do believe that you have been in a difficult situation, but you have not been threatened by the Office of the Prosecutor. There have been other forces that have been influencing you. The statements you have given to the Office of the Prosecutor are a true reflection of what you have been seeing and hearing, and for very unfortunate reasons you are now trying to backtrack from what you had earlier told the Office of the Prosecutor. Isn't that true, Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've turned everything upsidedown, topsy-turvy. Nobody threatened me. Well, somebody that you consider to be someone. I was threatened by the investigator, Rita Pradham, and I am repeating this for the tenth time, and I swear that that is so and I will take the solemn declaration once again, and I want legal proceedings to be taken against her, because as a person in a position of responsibility, she must be held responsible. If I was born in a village, I'm not a village goat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this concludes my examination. I would like to tender a number of documents at this point. Your Honours, it is my submission that the witness, as I have just put to him, gave correct statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2003 and 2006. Those statements reflect his true evidence. He is -- has not been testifying according to his statements and according to the truth on a number of occasions during his testimony and has retracted key parts of his evidence, such as whether or not Seselj's men participated in the attack on Zvornik, such as whether he ever had a meeting with the accused after he had been in Tenja, and a number of other things which I can go into if Your Honours want more detail, but in the interest of time, maybe I should move on. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please give us the numbers of the statements, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We're tendering the October 2006 statement which has 65 ter 07330. I would also like to tender the unsigned version of the witness's July statement from 2003, and that is the statement which was in tab -- under tab number 2 in the binder that I mentioned earlier, and the 65 ter number is 0462-6479, 0462-6500. The signed version of that statement we also tender. It's dated the 28th of September, 2003. It has 65 ter number 07327. We also tender the October 1st statement from 2007. The 65 ter number of that one is 07331. And the associated documents with that are 65 ter numbers 07332, 07334, 07335. And the version of the -- the statement to the Defence team which was later provided to the Office of the Prosecutor we also tender. It is 65 ter number 07333. We would also like to tender the statement from 2005 that the President read significant portions from to the witness. That is 65 ter number 07322 -- sorry, correction. 07329. And we have an investigator report about the witness's first meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor. That has 65 ter number 07328. And yesterday the President read out from a report prepared by Marie Costello of the Office of the Prosecutor about the witness's contact with the Office of the Prosecutor. It is the document in the blue binder or folder. That document does not have a 65 ter number or an ERN number, so we will be advising the Court of what 65 ter that declaration have as soon as possible just so there's no -- at least I gave a date. The date of the statement is the 7th of April, 2010. That was a fair bit in one go. I think I got it all. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. As you know -- one moment. As you know, Mr. Marcussen, the Trial Chamber will rule on this application after the cross-examination only. All of this is on the record. Mr. Seselj will have an hour and a half after this to cross-examine the witness. We shall have a break now. Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have half a minute with regard to what Mr. Marcussen said? First of all, I think I will need a little more time. I thought I'd need at least an hour and 45 minutes. That's the amount of time used by Mr. Marcussen. Secondly, what Mr. Marcussen has requested has no legal foundation. However, in certain cases, statements are directly tendered into evidence, but I'm discriminated against with regard to the accused in those cases. Judge Lattanzi's a member of a Chamber that's dealing with the Karadzic case, so she has witnessed this. I follow this by watching the Bijeljina television, and I can see that the Chamber takes witness statements into evidence, admits it into evidence, but then the Prosecution has an hour for its interrogation and the accused 10 or 12 hours. I am supposed to have the same amount of time as the Prosecution. I was brought here yesterday together with General Tolimir. He said that he usually had 10 or 12 hours to interview a witness. But what the witness said would be admitted into evidence, and then the Prosecution would interview the witness for an hour, an hour and a half. I'm just drawing your attention to what is happening in other cases. So I'm being discriminated against in comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do the same thing as you do. You look at the television, you see what's going on and I always watch my screen when I'm in my office, and I follow the Karadzic case, as well as the Tolimir case, and others. And I note that in other cases, just like here, it's always the same -- it's the same way of doing it. The Prosecution has a number of hours for its examination-in-chief and then we -- the Defence has the same time for the cross-examination. So the Prosecutor has used a bit more than an hour and 30 minutes, and you will also have a little bit more than an hour and 30 minutes. Of course, you also have administrative matters that you want to discuss. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think you are well informed. Madam Lattanzi can confirm this. Mr. Karadzic gets 10 or 12 hours per witness. The Chamber must bear in mind that the Prosecution is a lot more capable than an accused, as a rule, who is defending himself. The Prosecution has means at its disposal. I am powerless. I have to confront the Prosecution. I just wave my hand and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, don't talk nonsense. You are talking about the Karadzic case. I follow it also, just like you. There are open sessions, and I follow the open sessions. Mr. Karadzic does have a lot of time to put questions to the witnesses, but in the Karadzic case, the Prosecutor decided to switch to a 92 ter -- to Rule 92 ter. He's got statements, written statements, and then the Defence, i.e., Mr. Karadzic has time to cross-examine the witness because that's the 92 ter rule. We're not using this rule here in this case. We are not using rule 92 ter. Here we were a viva voce -- we have a Chamber witness and we gave everyone an hour and 30 minutes where we could have used up all the time, you know, for the Judges and Trial Chamber, only giving you five minutes to the Prosecution and five minutes to you. But we were very fair and square with you, you know. Witness, now, you've listened to all of this. Please rest for 20 minutes because after the break Mr. Seselj will be cross-examining you, and you need to be in good shape. We'll meet again in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm just on my feet very briefly. I would like the record to just reflect that during the break, maybe during the towards the end of my examination of the witness, the accused provided us with references to the two documents that you've been handed during the break, and our case manager has printed these documents out and provided them to the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovic, I would like most to deal with questions that are important in relation to the indictment brought against me. You allegedly in your statements, which the Prosecution has provided me with, naturally I believe you when you say that the Prosecution put suggestions to you with regard to the contents of the statement, but I believe that some of the things in the statements are some of the things you said, so I would now like to clarify this matter and see what is true and what isn't true in your statements. Here it says that you, in October 1991, set off with Dragan Spasojevic, and perhaps with Janko Lakic to Baranja to act as volunteers there with a large group of other men, I don't know how many of them there were, in order to gain war experience there as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that we did set off through the MUP so that young men who hadn't been in the battle-field would gain some wartime experience because the war in Bosnia was imminent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP of the Bosnian Serbs from Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Zvornik MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But at the time the MUP hadn't been split up into a Serb and Muslim component; is that right? Because that was in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it had already been divided, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As far as I know, it hadn't been divided by that time, but Dragan Spasojevic was also an SDS activist; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the president of the party, not the president, in fact, the secretary, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You set off there by bus; is that right? And in private cars.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you say that you were by -- near the village of Darda there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. So now you say that over there you had contact with Rade Kostic, who was a functionary of the police force of Serbian Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the deputy minister, Martic's deputy minister. He was responsible for Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The police there wore uniforms similar to the police force in Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. There were very slight differences, however the colour was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the colour of the uniforms was different. And there were other insignia with the Serbian flag; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were offered the possibility of working in the police, but you were to remove the insignia with a two-headed eagle as it was considered to be a Chetnik symbol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we didn't have any insignia with the two-headed eagle. We had police insignia, insignia worn by the police in the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. You then describe how you returned on the 27th of November, you returned home, and after several days Dragan Spasojevic called you again and asked you to report to him in the Zvornik SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was the police commander, whereas the chief of the secretariat of internal affairs was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's not important. It's not important. If I have understood this correctly, he engaged you as his body-guard on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And since he couldn't employ in the police where the Serbs and Muslims were together, you received your salary from the Serbian Democratic Party. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The salary was paid to you in the form of social benefit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you, together with Dragan Spasojevic, went to Baranja again from December 1991 until March 1992. You went to fetch weapons on three occasions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Baranja is in the Republic of Serbian Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was a weapons warehouse there near Beli Manastir or Darda, where would it be?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Darda, a little outside the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You usually went to fetch four or five lorries.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your statement, it says that you loaded firewood onto the lorries, firewood that was gathered as aid for the Serbs in Baranja because they didn't have many forests there and they didn't have wood; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But when you would arrive there, your statement says, Dragan Spasojevic apparently sold that firewood.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible because the lorries would arrive empty in Darda.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you would set off with firewood?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 56 on your statement from 2006, it says: "The lorries would go from Zvornik to Mali Zvornik, and then we would go to Croatia. We would cross the bridge. We moved -- we removed the insignia from the lorries. Dragan Spasojevic would then take the profit." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't believe you said Croatia. You probably said the Republic of Serbian Krajina, but since your interpreter was a Croat, she probably used a faulty version of the Serbian language and changed this, too, is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because Baranja was never part of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
