utterances.text: Now it's under Croatian occupation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You loaded weapons onto the lorries there and you would cover the weapons with sugar and other goods, food; is that correct? There were boxes and wine, and so on.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you covered it with that because you had to go through Serbia. You couldn't go from Baranja to Zvornik unless you went through Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First you have Zvezda and then Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were afraid that the Serbian police might stop you somewhere and in order to hide the weapons, you used flour, wine, sugar, and certain other goods; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that shows that as far as the authorities in Serbia are concerned, what you were doing was illegal. The authorities in Serbia wouldn't have allowed you to do this had they been aware of this?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If they had arrested us, we would have been accused of trafficking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Of trafficking in weapons. And you would have been held to account; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. And then you say how things transpired when you arrived in Zvornik with weapons, and you said how the weapons were distributed in Serbian villages. Were some of the weapons delivered to Muslims? Did they end up in hands of the Muslims? Were there Serbs who would sell weapons to Muslims instead of giving them to Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that from Muslims later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Muslims were fairly well armed at the time; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were well armed. But when the police would come to look for rifles, well, they would ask for a thousand German marks because a Serb sold them -- a weapon for a thousand marks. They said, Give me a thousand marks, I'll give you the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. So now we come to the conflict around Zvornik between the Serbian and the Muslim forces. You know that far before the conflict the Muslims formed the Green Berets paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they moved around Zvornik quite freely. They weren't armed, but they wore Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But is it correct to say that Muslim policemen, at the beginning of April, took away a large amount of weapons from the police warehouse and distributed them to the worst criminals in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among them there were criminals from Mali Zvornik, criminals who were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They went there, took the weapons and joined the paramilitary formation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They controlled the entrance over the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the time, did the Serbian civilians flee en masse? Most of the Serbs fled from Zvornik; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. I assisted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the policemen split up into Serbian and Muslim groups. The Serbs moved to Karakaj, the Serbian police moved to Karakaj which is a suburb of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And where is Radalj?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radalj is in Serbia, across the Drina River. It's three kilometres from the main road or from the Drina River. It's opposite Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How far is it in kilometres from Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about 8 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in Zvornik, prior to this conflict, both the Serbs and Muslims had their own Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And both Crisis Staffs were preparing for confrontation and sometimes they also tried to negotiate about how to divide the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at the beginning of April the vice-president of Republika Srpska came to Zvornik, Biljana Plavsic, and she attended a meeting of the Serbian Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the beginning of April, were you always together with Dragan Spasojevic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but sometimes I would stay by the car while he attended a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that under the influence of Biljana Plavsic the Crisis Staff took a decision, according to which Arkan should be paid to come to Zvornik and to participate in imminent fighting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know how much money was involved?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, but there was this deal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to the information presented here, the amount was about 300.000 German marks. Do you know that Dragan Spasojevic, the police commander, was made responsible by the Crisis Staff to go to Arkan and to hand over the money to him?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that, and I -- I've heard about that from him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with him after the war too?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He's a rich businessman in Serbian now, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. One of the richest ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And before the war, was he rich?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was a medical orderly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Our people would say he didn't have a penny.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But we're not talking about him here. We're interested in Arkan above all. When Arkan arrived from Bijeljina, he went to Radaljska Banja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He arrived with very few men.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, you know that a JNA unit had been deployed in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was that the tank brigade that arrived from Jastrebarsko in Croatia? It arrive in the territory of Tuzla and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the commander of the brigade was Colonel Tacic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that a tank battalion from that brigade was in Zvornik under the command of Dragan Obrenovic, Captain Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Dragan too. I saw him there. Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Dragan Obrenovic was included in the work of the Serbian Crisis Staff in Zvornik for a certain period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution has provided me with some documents that show that in addition to his officer's pay from the JNA, he would receive a salary as a member of the Crisis Staff. Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution provided me with this information. The Prosecution knows about this. When Arkan arrived in Zvornik, what day was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer. I can't remember the exact day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the Serbs had already fled from Zvornik, the Serbian civilians.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And many remained at the barricades. They couldn't flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And most of them fled to Serbia, to Mali Zvornik and beyond.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because prior to the operation for the liberation of Zvornik, the bridge was open for everyone who wanted to cross the river, for Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the JNA also had an Operative Group called the Drina group at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the command of the Operative Group was at Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What's Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Above Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The altitude is about 720 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the commander of the Drina Operative Group was Colonel Milosevic; is that correct? Have you ever heard of him?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Here we have a document that the Muslims drafted and a document that the Prosecution provided me with. It's dated the 31st of August, 1996. We have this handwritten date. I don't know what the exact source of the document is, but it's quite obvious that it was drafted by the Muslims. Do you have that document before you? Have you been provided with it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just change my glasses. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please, we'll deal with this will document at some length.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the title it says, "Chronology of events related to the aggression against Zvornik." Naturally, the Muslims provide their own version. They don't say how their police force aren't criminals, how they made the civilians afraid and caused them to flee. They don't say anything against themselves, naturally, but they are familiar with the events on the Serbian side. Perhaps certain things are incorrect. Perhaps certain things are correct, but I would like us to clarify a few questions in relation to that document. I have certain doubts about certain things here, but there are certain details that I'm interested in. Have a look at the third date on the first page, the 4th of April, 1992. The Muslim source says it must be the Muslim intelligence service or the AID. The Prosecution didn't really tell me who the body is that drafted the document. It says secret mobilisation and distribution of arms of the Territorial Defence forces in the municipalities in Mali Zvornik, Loznica, and their deployment at the initial position in preparation before an attack on Zvornik took place. Now was there any need for there to be secret mobilisation at all?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, need for it to be secret mobilisation because the sovereignty of Yugoslavia was being defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that partial mobilisation took place in the area of Mali Zvornik and Loznica at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Mali Zvornik and I do believe that it was done in Loznica, too, although I didn't go down there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well I know, you see. I know that some members of the Serbian Radical Party were mobilised too directly to the JNA. For example, Zoran Subotic was mobilised, and later on the JNA appointed him commander of the Territorial Defence in Zvornik. Did you hear that he was the commander of the Territorial Defence for a short time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I saw him once or twice, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He gave a statement to The Hague OTP where he describes the situation in detail. However, the Prosecution did not wish to call him as a witness because his statement doesn't suit them. Now, you see, I know that the reserve force of the police was raised as well. In Loznica, the reserve police force and several members of the Serbian Radical Party was mobilised at the time, and at the head, as commander, was Vojislav Jekic. Have you ever heard of him?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of him. He was a member of the state security, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As far as I know he was chief of the secretariat of internal affairs, but never mind, perhaps I'm wrong. So partial mobilisation took place. Now, if you think about it logically, why -- why was it necessary? Because the tank brigade did not have any infantry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it also right that Captain Obrenovic deployed his tanks to protect the bridges on the Drina River and the hydroelectric power plant there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So his entire battalion was deployed in that manner; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So could the JNA allow it to be thrown out of the Zvornik area by Muslim paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it could not allow that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that is why it is quite normal that the JNA was preparing to settle accounts with those Muslim paramilitaries; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, you see, towards the bottom of that page, the last date there is the 5th of April, 1992, and prior to that, before that month of April, the incident in Sapna took place where the Muslims stopped a military column and killed Stanojevic there, and several of our soldiers fled and people thought that they were killed first, so warrant officer -- warrant officer was killed there. Have you heard of that incident?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when the incident took place, that was a signal to the Serbs to prepare to settle accounts; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: "Now the Muslims," and towards the end of the page it says, "by using the aforementioned incident, the prepared separation of the Serbian police was undertaken and their police moved to the premises of the Alhos company in Karakaj." I assume that that is correct; right? That the Serb policemen left, but not only because of the indent that took place, but also because criminals in Zvornik had become armed?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they were afraid for their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So several hundred people there were armed on that day; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, it says here the Muslim sources say that the roads were obstructed, the road between Zvornik and Karakaj, Zvornik Sapota [phoen], Zvornik Sapna, and between Zvornik, Sepak, and Pilica. Chetnik barricades were set up by members of Arkan's and Seselj's forces. Now they call -- they refer to Arkan as a Chetnik as well; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was just having a bit of a laugh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you take care that that -- that you don't make that noise with the documents waiving them in front of the microphone.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now they say here where Arkan's forces were and where Seselj's men were at their initial positions. Of course they say Seselj formations which means the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party who arrived from Belgrade right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they say that they had their bases in Radalj and Mali Zvornik. And as for the Arkan's men, we know that they were in Radalj. And I personally know about the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party that they were stationed in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. And there were also members of the Serbian militia there, they say the JNA, and as they also say, paramilitary forces of the Serbian Democratic Party. Now, since we know that between Radalj and Mali Zvornik there's a distance of 8 kilometres, let's see which location would be -- would involve Arkan's men and where the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party could be deployed. Arkan's men might have been along the Zvornik Karakaj road; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were even further. They were in Radaljska Banja, the spa, which is 16 or 15 kilometres aware from Zvornik because it's 8 kilometres from Radalj to Mali Zvornik, and then Radaljska Banja is 7 kilometres further off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So where could they set up these blockades along the roads?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody. Nowhere. How could they set up blocks in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, not in Serbia. They moved from Radalj to Zvornik area, I assume.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, they did move, but I just said that they were stationed up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So nowhere along those roads, Zvornik, Karakaj, Zvornik Sapa [phoen], Zvornik Sapna, Pilica, it isn't possible that Arkan's men were there at all; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No Arkan's men anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you could have had the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and the JNA. And the volunteers of the Serbian Democratic Party and the Serbian militia; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now we come to -- well, it goes on to talk about certain other events viewed from the Muslim angle of vision which isn't particularly interested as far as we're concerned. And we come to the 8th of April. Is that when negotiations were underway between the Serbian and Muslim Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that was in the morning, was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They divided Zvornik -- well, there's the river Zlatica and that was the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that when Arkan stormed into the meeting and started to slap the Serbian members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did he slap Brano Grujic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He probably slapped them all because he told me to go outside and there was a lot of shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It seems that he slapped Captain Dragan Obrenovic from the JNA, just not Dragan Spasojevic, otherwise he slapped around everybody else?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because Dragan Spasojevic brought him money; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the members of the Crisis Staff who took part in collecting money for Arkan and in calling Arkan in, persuaded to do so by Biljana Plavsic, they were slapped?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, they deserved it for having called Arkan in in the first place?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, the Muslims go on to say and look at page 3 for that, the third date there, the 8th of April. From the early morning hours an attack by Arkan's men started at positions organised by defenders in the area of Vratolomac, Debelo Brdo, and Kazanbasca. Do you know which area that is because I don't know the region very well, where is that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's at the entrance to Karakaj in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it's between Karakaj and Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have Vratolomac is a hill on the right-hand side and then you have Kazanbasca which is lower down. It's a settlement lower down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So what I said earlier on that Arkan's men were only along the Karakaj-Zvornik access is corrects, and that they were at the Karakaj barricades, but not many of them, just some 30 men right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts, about 30, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Arkan's men attacked, and together with them, there were some policemen, Serb policemen from Zvornik, and you were there, too, as far as I can see from your statement; is that right, were you there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, were they there with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday, and I repeated today that they weren't. And I said this on oath, but nobody seems to take -- taken any notice of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, how come then in this alleged statement of yours, and it's paragraph 92 from the 2006 statement, you say about 40 -- some 40 Arkan's men, some 15 Serbian policemen from Bosnia-Herzegovina, and up to 50 Seselj's Chetniks attacked the town of Zvornik. There were between 100 and 120 people in total. I'm surprised to see that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again, that's an interpretation made by the investigator Rita Pradham, because I said that there were people there with insignias and cockades, the locals of Karakaj and Zvornik whom I knew personally, who did not belong -- they were in the SDS. Some of them didn't belong to anybody. They had no uniforms. They had nothing, but they set out anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, look at the last sentence in that paragraph. Do you have your statement in front of you? Perhaps it will help you if you take a look at the statement and perhaps the Tribunal Officer will help you there. It says: "Seselj's Chetniks wore civilian clothes, the sajkaca type of cap and cockades on them?" Now, how come Seselj's Chetniks were wearing civilian clothes I ask you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was -- seemed funny to me because your men, your volunteers, all belonged to the army, and they were given uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Only when you went as a volunteer in the summer of 1991, while the JNA had not yet taken part in the war and when we sent men on our own initiative, that's when we had a shortage of uniforms; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party a little less than 100 of them, in -- came to Zvornik wearing new camouflage JNA uniforms, brand new, directly supplied by the Bubanj Potok people and came to Mali Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they arrived in Mali Zvornik, and I know that they were over there, but I wasn't able to distinguish between soldiers and Seselj volunteers. I couldn't know who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First of all, you couldn't have differentiated Seselj's volunteers from the other JNA soldiers; is that right? Let's get things clear.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Except by the cockades they wore on their caps.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They put -- everybody wore cockades, civilians, soldiers, everybody liked the cockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, everybody liked the cockade, and you said yesterday very clearly that the cockade is incorporated into the official Serbian flag today.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. We're not challenging or debating that, but I seem to have the impression from this statement of yours, alleged statement, I don't know how far you took part in the writing of it, but it seems to me that you depicted the fact as follows: That Arkan led the attack on Zvornik. Did you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I said. I said that Arkan led his own unit. He was in command of his own unit in the operation to liberate Zvornik, and maybe some of the locals who had joined in saw him on the road and then joined him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But I gained the impression that yesterday you were saying that it was the Crisis Staff of Zvornik who -- which commanded the Serb forces. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, how can it be correct? Who of those members of the Crisis Staff were capable of commanding, for instance? Is Dragan Spasojevic capable of commanding a unit or anybody else, any other member of the Crisis Staff, for example?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think Dragan Spasojevic could have been capable of doing that. There was Obrenovic in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For us to make things clearer, we're going to refer to our brethren the Muslims again, because they seem to know the situation better than we do, and here is what they say: "On the 8th of April," and you'll find that on page 3, the third date, "from the early morning hours an attack was launched by Arkan's men across positions organised hastily by the defenders in the area of Vratolomac, Debelo Brdo and Kazanbasca. Although poorly armed and with minimum quantities of ammunition, the defenders," that means the Muslim soldiers, "put up fierce resistance and the attackers suffered significant casualties. So Arkan, himself, in the early morning of the 8th of April set out to attack and was defeated." That's what the Muslims say. Do you remember that? You were with that unit of his. Arkan wasn't capable of commanding anything. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember the attack first of all, they used mortars and then they set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's get one thing clear. Arkan had many courageous men in his unit but no capable officers. So how could he lead a whole attack on Zvornik and how could Zvornik be taken by only 120 Serbian soldiers? Zvornik is not a small town. How many inhabitants does Zvornik have? How many did it have in 1991, for example?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm really not good with figures. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. The Muslims go on to say that Arkan was defeated, that he suffered considerable losses. Do you remember that some Serbs were killed, that there were casualties on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were casualties but not any of Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But there were other casualties, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I brought in a man who was wounded and he died of the wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you couldn't have been a Seselj man, yourself, could you? You weren't one of Arkan's men either, but you took part in the attack with them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I couldn't have been one of Seselj's men, and I told you why. I didn't belong to any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here that you went into the attack, that there were five Arkan's men and then five of you and then another five Arkan's men and about 24 groups with five men in each group. Now, where did Arkan gain this military skill, that is to say, to send five people on the attack? Did he go to the military academy in Russia [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, aren't you aware that you had a highly incapable set of commanders?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult to enter into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the Muslims go on to say, and this is the fifth date: "An all-out attack on Zvornik began at 1500 hours with artillery fire of the JNA armoured mechanised battalion and fire coming from the armed groups of the Territorial Defences of Serbia, Mali Zvornik, and Loznica." Right. So it's the JNA setting out at 3.00 in the afternoon now. So Arkan launched an attack himself alone. He wants to show that he was a brave man and deserved the money he was given, and he set out and launched an attack without any co-ordination with the JNA, because there was Colonel Tacic, a commander of the tank brigade on the JNA side, and Commander Milosevic, Colonel Milosevic, of the Drina group; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it was Colonel Tacic's group and Dragan Obrenovic with a tank battalion; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to intervene, Mr. Seselj. I was trying to understand why you were putting your questions and for what purpose. I noticed, Witness, that in the statement you gave in 2003, if the statement is true, which is Mr. Marcussen's theory, if we assume that the statement is true, how is it then, Witness, that in paragraph 86 of the statement - you don't need to look at it, I have it before me - you say that the attack on Zvornik was conducted by Arkan's men, a few policemen, 15 officers, and people from the Territorial Defence, but at no point in time do you talk about the JNA when we know that the artillery's there. How is that, Witness? How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because Arkan's men started attacking very early, and as Mr. Seselj said, they were defeated and they returned. No one then asked me to explain the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, what I'm interested in is the following: The Muslims -- to helped us to show that there were two attacks, there was the failed Arkan attack, and you also participated. There were Serbian policemen who participated, and members -- Serb members of the Territorial Defence, local inhabitants of Zvornik. You were defeated. You suffered significant casualties. Your command structure wasn't professional, and Arkan did not co-ordinate his efforts with the JNA. That's what I'm interested in; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the JNA launched its attack together with the volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party, there was also the Beli Orlovi or the White Eagles group. There was the reserve police force from Loznica, there were members from the Territorial Defence from Loznica and Mali Zvornik, but we're talking about members of the JUG Operative Group, and of members of the tank brigade. When the JNA launched its attack together with our volunteers, then the Muslim defence of Zvornik was completely routed. The Muslim forces started fleeing, and by night Zvornik was liberated; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Arkan entered Zvornik, too. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He entered with his 30 men, and he went to the Hrid settlement. Have you heard about that place?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution has stated in its indictment that that is where Arkan's men killed about 20 Muslim civilians. Have you heard about that crime?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about it, and I followed the trial when you were charged with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You found out about this from the case against me; is that correct? You didn't know about it before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about it earlier on too, but I also followed the trial when there was a protected witness, a woman who testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A Muslim woman testified here Arkan's men killed her husband and two sons, and she quite clearly distinguished between Arkan's men and Seselj's men. However, on one occasion she said, They are all the same for us, but she quite clearly said that Arkan's men would shoot people, whereas Seselj's men would give children sweets. Why am I insisting on this? Because I want to get Arkan off my back and I want to demonstrate for the benefit of the Trial Chamber that Arkan didn't participate in the fight for Zvornik together with the same formations with which volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party were fighting. The Serbian Radical Party volunteers were with the JNA. As the Muslim source says, they launched an attack on the 8th of April in the afternoon. In the morning, Arkan led a failed attack. He was defeated. He returned to his initial position. And when Zvornik was liberated, he entered the town and started looting it and killing; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since Arkan did manage to justify the amount of money that had been paid to him by the Crisis Staff he tried to attack the town of Kula as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He set off again with you, I don't know whether you were there personally, but he set off with local inhabitants from -- you people from Mali Zvornik, in the certain sense, inhabitants although there is the Drina separating you. He set off with his men and some members of the police force and members of the Territorial Defence and when he entered Kula, he was defeated again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it also correct to say that at that time some important men of his were killed.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Rambo and Zika.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were then killed in the attack on the town of Kula.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When hearing another witness here I quoted a statement made by Colonel Tacic. Colonel Tacic informed me of this statement and this shows that he personally asked the General Staff in Belgrade to have Arkan and his men driven out of Zvornik. Do you know that two or three days later Arkan had to leave Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that JNA commanders immediately launched an investigates into the crimes committed against Muslim civilians in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the then Colonel Stankovic from the Military Medical Academy was at the head of the forensic team. He's a pathologist and he started doing autopsies of the killed civilians?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think his name was Zoran Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Zoran Stankovic later became a general. He was the chief of the Military Academy. He was even in the Ministry of Defence for a certain period of time. He testified in open session in court and he testified about the investigates that was launched. So the JNA's intention was to launch an investigates into Arkan's activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally they wouldn't have called a pathologist if their intention wasn't to launch an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All the bodies were examined, the cause of death was established, other forensic measures were taken. However is it true to say that there were several hundred Muslims who had been killed there? That's what it says in your statement.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well that's not true for sure, because in peacetime you never see anyone dead and then all of a sudden you see a lot of dead people, and so our hair stood on end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Paragraph 101 of your statement, it says there between 200 and 300 dead bodies of Muslims who had been killed on the attack on Zvornik, according to all the information that I have.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It couldn't have been such a number.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When Arkan's men left Zvornik, the Serbian forces massed around the town of Kula.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The JNA forces were there and the Serbian Radical Party volunteers were there, as well as Serbian policemen, members of the Territorial Defence, and so on and so forth. However, they didn't have a capable commander who could have led the attack successfully.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but I was on leave when there was this operation to liberate Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. I will, in that case, provide you with another piece of information. Since the Serbian forces were not in a position to take the town of Kula because of its exceptionally good strategic position, you know there's a large fortress there, medieval one, it's very difficult terrain, and the Muslims who were well armed were there and managed to defend themselves successfully; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then the command of the first army, as the Prosecution put it, the commander of the 1st Army, Captain Dragan Obrenovic, who was on trial here then struck a deal, and so on and so forth, but he said certain things that are true. The command of the 1st Army ordered the special forces to assist the Serbian forces in Zvornik and the then Milorad Stupar, who subsequently became a colonel, arrived and his unit was a protective regiment from the 1st Army. That's a special unit. Have you heard about that? Have you heard about Stupar?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I've seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Dragan Obrenovic told The Hague Prosecution that the attack on Kula at the end of April was planned by Stupar from the JNA, the Territorial Defence of Zvornik, and by certain Serbian paramilitary formations that were there at the time. He mentions the White Eagles, Zuci's men and Privaja [phoen] unit. Dragan Obrenovic doesn't mention the Serbian radicals. He avoided mentioning my name too, for some reason, but it's quite obvious that Colonel Stupar organised all the Serbian forces. They weren't paramilitary formations. They were volunteers who were part of the JNA and decisive attack was launched. And it was carried out so well that the town of Kula was soon taken. The Muslims were dispersed. They fled, and they didn't have significant casualties. Perhaps three or four. No more than that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ten, three, or five casualties, I don't know exactly, but they left their positions and went towards Lipje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We're talking about people so we won't say ten pieces, ten people died in the course of the battle. We won't call our enemy a piece. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with you. A victim is a victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In any event, they died in battle.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What I am now interested in is as follows: How is it that in paragraph 120 of your statement it says that in the course of the attack on Kula, well you say at the time you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But here it says you were. You say, allegedly, this is what the statement says, our objectives were not to take any prisoners. That means the objective was to kill as many people as possible or to force them to go to the end of the village where other units were positioned for shooting. Our goal was to frighten them. The population from Kula Grad had nowhere to run to except towards Lipje, right into the hands of the units that were waiting to shoot at them. On page -- in paragraph 121, it says: "My unit," although you weren't there, it says, "My unit was to wait for the signal to shoot at the house in Kula. We were not allowed to leave our positions."

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That just proves the truth of what I was saying, but I was told that I wasn't telling the truth. This is Rita Pradham's interpretation. I know for sure, and this can be confirmed by ten witnesses that I was in Novi Sad. I spent four or five days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 123 it says that after the attack on the town of Kula you took leave for a week. You said you were going to visit your sick child.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here "after the attack."

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the attack on Kula. Before the operation to liberate the town of Kula I went to Novi Sad to have a rest with my sister-in-law because I was exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here it says that you also participated in the attack on the town of Kula, but that's not correct because you didn't.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wasn't possible from Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So how is it that this is in your statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how can I explain it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of a Muslim civilian being killed in the course of the Serbian attack on Kula? We have concluded that perhaps ten Muslim combatants were killed, but I doubt it was ten. It was probably fewer than ten, according to the information I have. But are you aware of a single civilian being killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard about that. I heard that they fled, the civilians fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When they saw how professionally this well-planned attack had been carried out, they first fled. First the Muslim soldiers fled from their positions and then they were followed by the civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what my colleagues, other policemen, told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So in the course of taking the town of Kula, no war crimes were committed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a hundred per cent true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the course of the month of April, up until the 26th of April, are you aware of anyone else killing Muslim civilians or prisoners in Zvornik, anyone apart from Arkan, in the settlement of Hrid?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution wasn't aware of that either so they couldn't state any anything to that effect in my indictment. They only mentioned Arkan's killings in the Hrid settlement. We had eyewitnesses with whom we could check this detail at least. Very well. Now, after the fall of the town of Kula, after that significant Muslim fortification fell, do you know that JNA infantry units withdrew to Serbia? Do you know that Colonel Stupar's unit left, that Serbian Radical Party volunteers withdrew?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbian Radical Party volunteers withdrew after the operation to liberate Kula. Stupar's men withdrew. I know that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then a normal situation was to be established in Zvornik, civilian authorities and a Territorial Defence was to be established. The town was to function normally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Perhaps not call the Serbian Radical Party volunteers withdrew. Perhaps a few decided to stay on. I am familiar with one example, a certain Slavkovic who went on trial in Belgrade as a member of the Pivarski unit or the Yellow Wasp unit. He said that he went there as a member of the Serbian Radical Party volunteers, but after the 26th of April he remained on -- he stayed on in Zvornik. Do you know that after the 26th of April, a Territorial Defence was formed that was composed of various volunteers and its name was Igor Markovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that on that occasion Vojin Vuckovic Zuco was appointed pursuant to a decision of the Crisis Staff. He was appointed as commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the first time I saw him was when I came from Novi Sad. I saw him and his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have Vojin Vuckovic's statement, Vojin Vuckovic Zuco's statement too in which he describes his arrival in Zvornik together with Legija Miroslav Bogdanovic and his brother Dusan describes an arrest by the Muslims, and so on. He wasn't in command of a unit of any kind prior to the 26th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So is it possible that he had command over Serbian Radical Party volunteers then? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would that be possible since he wasn't a member of that party?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here you say that you saw how Zuco was giving a speech to the Chetniks, but that could only have been after the 26th of April. Then he could have given a speech to members of his own unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was an interpretation, Zuco holding a speech. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's what it says in your statement.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't say that. There's lots -- there are lots of things in my statement which I never said. I suppose they thought I was a semi-literate and then they just wrote down whatever they felt like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does that mean that none of the statements that you gave to The Hague Tribunal can be treated as being true and correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, because I know what the truth is and what it wasn't the truth, but it cannot be treated as being accurate, because some things didn't happen and I know that they didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, what Mr. Marcussen, The Hague Prosecutor put to you at the end of his examination when he said that the statements are a true rendition of what you saw and heard, is that nonsense?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is it. I have a doctor behind me here and I had to take some pills.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, the Muslim sources have shown us that it's all nonsense, because the facts, according to the Muslim sources, are different. So the Muslims have helped us to clarify, once and for all, Arkan's role and the role of the JNA and all the other formations led by the JNA and under its command. They have clarified this in great detail very precisely and I'm grateful to them for having done that. Now in the indictment raised against me, I am being accused and charged of being responsible for Arkan's executions in Hrid. Then the crimes committed in the Standard factory are mentioned. Are you heard of those crimes?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, your unit was never there. Your unit was never in the Standard company. It was never stationed there. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So if crimes occurred there, they occurred in May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know about the crimes committed in Ciglana, that there was a group of prisoners there, incarcerated there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that. I never went down there, but I did hear about it. As a policeman I never went down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about the Ekonomija, the farm? Where is that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the right of Ciglana, and I went there only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the Ekonomija, the farm?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police were there at the entrance. The blue civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it possible that some volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party committed crimes at the Ekonomija?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's impossible. First of all, because the police provided security there and the volunteers, the Serbian Radical Party volunteers were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then it says in the indictment that I was responsible for the crimes in Drinjaca at the cultural centre there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've heard of everything. I followed the trial and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English transcript there is something missing. Line 10, page74, the witness said volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were disciplined, and it says were, and it says "..." It will be corrected later on. Go ahead. Continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said they were disciplined.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, in the indictment -- in the indictment crimes in Celopek are mentioned. Can they be brought into -- can they be connected to me in any way?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because in Celopek there was a detention unit there, and people were exchanged from there, Muslims. They were exchanged for Serbs, for our people. So I don't know whether there were any crimes there, but you couldn't ascribe those crimes to the Serbian Radical Party because the police in blue, the civilian police force were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, you mentioned a number of times Janko Lakic here.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that sometime in 2004 or 2005, I'm not quite sure which year, in Mali Zvornik rumours went round that Janko Lakic had become a witness of The Hague Tribunal and that he travelled abroad because of that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about that, and I read something like that in the papers. There was an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, he gave an extensive interview.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a photograph of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I provided a photocopy of that paper here. I'm not going to show it now again. Janko Lakic, at one point in time, decided on his own initiative to address the public and to say that he did not want to be a witness, Carla's witness, he said, I don't want to be a safe slave of Carla Del Ponte. Now, do you know that members of the team helping out my Defence, before 2007, never came into contact with anybody for whom we knew was a witness of The Hague Tribunal? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you also know, are you aware that in 2007, we collected statements from people who were interviewed by The Hague Prosecutor and who refused to come in and be witnesses like Jovo Ostojic, for example. I'm sure you heard of him, Slavoljub Jovanovic, Srecko Radovanovic, and many, many others.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that we published their statements in my book called "The Hague Instrumentalisation of False Witnesses." Have you heard of that book of mine?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then we started to promote that book in all of Serbia's municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was a book promotion in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's what I was about to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you know what happened then? Many of those who were on the list as Hague witnesses contacted my associates and said, yes, similar things happened to us and we're not going to testify for the Prosecution. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Janko Lakic also contacted my associates. He used to be a member of the Serbian Radical Party in 1990 when that brawl broke out at our rally in Mali Zvornik. You remember that, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but could --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was a promotional rally of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, because the Serbian Radical Party hadn't been established yet.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was in the first days of August. You said that it was in May or June, but it was actually the beginning of August. We wore short-sleeved shirts. I personally had a shirt with short sleeves and I was wearing white jeans because I was a younger man so I could wear jeans at the time. Yes. I was working as a waiter. I had black trousers and a short-sleeved shirt, but I'm not good on dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However when, the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina there were members of our party from Mali Zvornik who crossed over to Veliki Zvornik and took part in the fighting there. Some of them became employed in the police force, others in the municipality and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some got married over there. Lots of things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Janko Lakic was some sort of officer over there, I believe, as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, he was a security officer of some kind, attached to some army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when he addressed the public Janko Lakic came into contact with members of my team and made a statement for them and described how they allegedly mistreated him, The Hague Prosecutor and investigators, and so on, but look what happened next. He expected us, I mean my team and the Serbian Radical Party as well, which in a way provides logistical support to my Defence team, some tangible benefit from that. Do you -- are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was probably his aim in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when we told him quite clearly that he would have no material gain from us and could expect none, he once again contacted The Hague OTP. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, it seems that the Prosecutor didn't believe him either so we -- The Hague -- The Hague OTP and I found ourselves along the same lines, because we realised that he was lying and we rejected him. The Prosecutor didn't want to become compromised through him, and I didn't want to waste my time on witnesses like that because it's not my aim to hear lies told here. And then Janko Lakic became a film star of the B92 television station in a programme with Natasa Kandic. He made various statements, and so on and so on and so forth. Did you watch that programme, the television programme?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that's what happened with Janko Lakic. Now, The Hague OTP, under Rule 48.1, provided me with another Muslim document, and I have to emphasise that it is a document from a Muslim source because it doesn't say here who compiled this document whereas it should say that. It is certificate 607 that I received from The Hague Prosecutor's office. It just says a list of those responsible for war crimes in Zvornik -- in the Zvornik region. We see that it comes from a Muslim source, but we have nothing to indicate what source that is precisely. Now, I'd like to ask you to take a look at page 1 of that document where it says persons responsible for war crimes in the Zvornik region, and then you have a list of names, only names, and under number 1 is Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Dusan Repic, that's Dusan Ruckovic [phoen], nicknamed Repic. Then number 3 is Dragan Spasojevic, the police commander; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to mention the names of the other people, but just take a look at the list yourself. I assume that the Judges have the list in front of them and so does the Prosecutor. The list is from 1 to 23, although there are many more names, because several names are mentioned under some of the numbers. Now, take a look at the list and tell us whether there's anybody there who's a member of the Serbian Radical Party, from 1 to 23.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see any member of the Serbian Radical Party here, but I do see under number 11 a man who is completely incapable. He wasn't even capable of walking. I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you mentioned some life on this document. Look at number 18. A person called Milenko Mijic, and it seems that is he's a judge, which is what drew my attention. He's a judge from Zvornik. And he became head of the police and organised the exodus of the population, et cetera, et cetera. Did you know this person, this Milenko Mijic, judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a time he was the chief of SUP in Zvornik, in Republika Srpska, in Bosnia, I mean, in Veliki Zvornik, in Bosnia. That's why I know him. I don't know anything else about him though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Did you know that he was a judge, that he had been a judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I really don't. I would say if I did. I know the man above him, too, under number 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I intentionally did not want to read out all the names on that list, because I assumed that were I to do so we were to call out people's name publicly and some of them probably had nothing to do with any crimes. You recognised Bozo Vidovic. I'm sure there are others, so that's why I don't want to read out the whole list and abuse people that way. All I'm interested in is to hear that you are certain that on that entire list there is nobody there from the Serbian Radical Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody. Mostly there are Serbs from Republika Srpska, from the present Republika Srpska. For example, the man I said was completely incapable of doing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Arkan's mentioned here. He's not from Zvornik. Dusan Vuckovic Repic who isn't and some others who aren't. They are generally known personages. Dragan Obrenovic is even mentioned. Now, would you turn the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, listen to Mr. Seselj. On one item he's absolutely right, saying there are names he does not want to mention. In this document there are some people who are found guilty and other where nothing is stated. So there's a presumption of innocent -- of innocence, but they are on a list mentioned on a list of people who were suppose -- allegedly responsible, but of course you could be allegedly responsible and in the end be acquitted. Mr. Witness, have you understood what I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I said was number 17. I didn't mention the name. I just said number 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me how much more time I have left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not much, Mr. Seselj. The Registrar will tell you. Twenty minutes ago the Registrar told me that you had 40 minutes left. So I believe you have between 20 or 25 minutes left, but go on and I will tell you exactly where we stand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you imagine, Mr. President, if Mrs. Lattanzi was well disposed towards me as she is towards Mr. Karadzic and give me 12 hours, all the magical things I could do here in this courtroom, but what can I do, things are as they are. I have to come to terms with my fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now could you look at page 3 of this document, please. It's the only place in the whole document where Seselj's men are mentioned. Under number 14 it says Drago Krstanovic and Matija Boskovic from Zvornik joined Seselj's formations and served as informers, making lists with the names of distinguished Bosniaks to be liquidated or forced to leave. So joined and then no specifics whether they actually ratted on someone as informers, whether someone was really liquidated or forced to leave. So this is not very serious; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not serious at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know Matija Boskovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes he's died since.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is he from Mali Zvornik or Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Zvornik, in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was later a member Serbian Radical Party; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps later on when I wasn't there any more when what happened to me happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, but never mind, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we'll have the break at a quarter to 6.00, so we'll still have 15 minutes to go. And since the Prosecutor used an hour and 40 minutes, you will have an additional 15 minutes for the witness. So you will have altogether an hour and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Judge. I reckon that I will need at least 20 minutes for administrative issues so that -- please bear that in mind. And warn me in time when we move closer to that point. I would like to ask some questions to this witness, although the essentials have already been discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jovic, we are going back to the part which is not relevant for this indictment and where you describe your departure, actually your only departure in the capacity of a volunteer of the SRS to the front line; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here that -- that you arrived at the staff of the Serbian Chetnik Movement or the headquarters of the Serbian Radical Party at Francuska Street and that you sat there with me. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I didn't know Belgrade at the time and I don't know it well now either. I don't know. It wasn't Francuska Street. I don't know what street it was and I didn't sit with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party had its seat in Francuska Street only as of September 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. As far as I know, it was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in the summer of 1991, our seat was in a rented apartment on the ground floor in -- on the Milutina Bojica Street. Does this jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A bit down the road from the Federal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it was on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And there were only two offices; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In one, the volunteers would gather if they were getting ready to leave, and in the other there was my office where my secretary sat and the vice-presidents of the party and other officials, and we had very small premises, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your alleged statement from 2006, we read that our volunteers addressed each other as major, colonel, or using other ranks. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard as much, but perhaps that -- those were not ranks. Maybe they were joking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Only one had the rank of major, Milan Dosijevic, Oliver Denis, from Baret, was captain, and there were some lieutenants who were promoted personally by Vojvoda Momcilo Djuic, and his order was read out publicly at the rally on Ravna Gora in 1991, in May, on the occasion of the great victory of our volunteers at Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, 1991. Nobody else had ranks; am I right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are 100 per cent right. Now I can see that -- that I heard what is really true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 19, we can read that there was talk of Greater Serbia, that Vojvoda Momcilo Djuic, from the USA, transferred his tile to Seselj and that he gave authorised Seselj to perform his duties from then on. Is anything like that possible at all? He promoted me to the rank of Vojvoda, but he didn't transfer his title to me. He died with his title.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And some malicious people said that he took away that title from me later on, although that's not true. Although pressurised by the American authorities, he said that he would take away that title from me, but he never did and he couldn't either.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can -- you can promote somebody to the rank of Chetnik Vojvoda in the homeland when there is no Chetnik Vojvoda there, but you can't take that title away from anyone from California, is that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 20, we read that I said that the SSCP would take care of you, transport the wounded to hospitals, and that the SSCP was going to take care of our medical and social insurance. This is impossible in practical terms. How, at that time, in the summer of 1991, when we had to hide from Milosevic's regime in Serbia, we crossed the Danube to go to Slavonia, how could we guarantee social insurance and medical insurance to you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you were not a firm who could have done that. That's not true. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You saw that there weren't even enough uniforms. The uniforms that we were able to find were old and worn, and so on. And that was like that until the 1st of October, 1991 when the state of imminent threat of war was proclaimed and we joined the units of the JNA. Then the JNA provided our fighters with the best uniforms and the best infantry weapons, and it never happened anywhere that any volunteer of the SRS indicted in Croatia or in the Republic of Serbian Krajina or the Republika Srpska or the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina or in Serbia, nowhere were they indicted of any particular war crime; am I right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And here's the million dollar question for the ICTY: Find one single volunteer of the SRS who has been indicted anywhere for any particular war crime. Of course, the OTP would like me to be a criminal. I may be a criminal by character. I may be a criminal based on my abilities to be better than the OTP, but anything more tangible than that they are unable to find; am I right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you came to Belgrade for the first time, you had problems because you had to wait for three days to be transported over the Danube; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We were all facing huge problems at the time because Milosevic's police tried to prevent us from crossing the Danube. So we crossed by ferries at certain points and in various ways, but sometimes we couldn't transport the volunteers over the Danube. They had come to Belgrade and we had to return them to their homes; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. So you did go to Tenja after all, and yesterday you gave a description of what happened in Tenja, where you corrected many things from your alleged statement. I don't really want to dwell on that for a long time. Do you know that I came to Tenja in the summer of 1991 on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but we had information that you would come to see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You may have not -- you may not have been there when I came. Is the Tenja the closest Serb village to Osijek, actual think a suburb of Osijek?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is close to the Saponia factory. It's only a stone's throw away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: While you were in Tenja, did everybody live there peacefully including Croats? Nobody bothered them and some Croats were members of the Serb TO of Tenja. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, Mr. Seselj. And I claim with full responsibility that in our unit there were Croats. I can mention their names but maybe not because they might face problems with their own people back there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, don't state their names.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I won't. But why should anybody expel their daughters, or children and women.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know what surprises me in paragraph 35? You allegedly say that there were other units of the Serbian Chetnik movement in Tenja when you -- when you arrive. One of the commanders of the Chetnik volunteers in Tenja, I remember, was Drecun, whose full name I don't know. That's probably Vukan Drecun.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I were to put to you now that Vukan Drecun belonged to an illegal organisation that called itself Black Hand, and which planned to kill me in 1991, and they attacked me once in the Ruskica [phoen] restaurant while I was giving an interview to a Muslim journalist from Sarajevo who worked for the "Nasi Dani" magazine. It was in April 1991. And he describes the entire incident in that magazine. Three guys attacked me, I hit two of them, the third one hit me with a chair from behind but -- and then all three of them ran away. I was a young man then and I was able to defend myself.
