How could Vukan Drecun have been a commander of a volunteer unit of the Serbian Radical Party? That's impossible.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I only saw him. I didn't say that he belonged to the Serbian Radical Party or anything. I just saw him. And somebody told me something like, There are some Chetniks over there. They live in that house up there, so we didn't have any contact at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So you're not sure that he may have been our volunteer. Is it correct, though, that the Serb opponents -- that the enemies of the Serbs called all Serb fighters Chetniks? Even Arkan was called a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Even my 11-year-old son may be called a Chetnik any time soon. In every statement of mine you will find the word "Chetnik" all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the term Chetnik would be a generic term here, including all sorts of things, and the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, the volunteers that the Serbian Radical Party from Belgrade through its War Staff sent to the front were -- were the ones; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So even morally I would be responsible only for those who I sent to war from Belgrade, and if they committed any crime, God forbid, but there is not information that they did.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And I'm glad there is no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So if you heard of any volunteers of the SRS having committed a crime, please say so.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But I did hear that in Zvornik they gave chocolate to the children there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What happened now? It's time for a break anyway. Judges, I have basically finished this cross-examination. Although I haven't used all my time. It is very important to me to deal with administrative matters so I can now finish with this witness for good, because all I could do would be a repetition -- would be more of the same, but only slightly different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will have a 20-minute break, and after the break you'll have about 15 minutes if you want to continue putting questions to the witness, and I'll ask Mr. Marcussen if he has redirect, and then you can deal with the administrative matters. We have a 20-minute break first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Mr. Marcussen has no additional questions and I see him waving his head, then we can release the witness, and then right after the break I can move on to administrative matters, unless Mr. Marcussen has anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can release the witness, but I'll tell him later on. We have to thank him first before releasing him. I hope that the connection with Belgrade will be up again, but since many miracles have happened today, we'll just hope for a new miracle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. We can see the witness on the screen. Mr. Seselj, you have no further questions to put to the witness, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have, in fact, completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Witness, on behalf of my colleagues I would like to thank you for having come to testify via videolink notwithstanding your state of health, and for two days you have answered questions put to you by the Bench, by the Prosecutor and by Mr. Seselj. So we would like to thank you for having come as a court witness at the request of the Trial Chamber to establish the truth. I wish you all best. I hope your health will improve over the next few days, and I hope all goes well in whatever you undertake in the future. I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the room in which you find yourself at the moment. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The two documents which did not have 65 ter numbers when I tendered them have now been given 65 ter numbers thanks to the kind assistance of our case manager and the court staff. The unsigned version of the witness's 2003 statement from July that I mentioned has been given 65 ter number 07544, and the declaration by Prosecution investigator Marie Costello, dated 7th of April, 2010, has been given 65 ter number 07545.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Seselj, I will give you the floor to address housekeeping matters. One moment. Before you take the floor, Mr. Seselj, as far as what you said yesterday is concerned, I have something to say about it. When you mentioned Rule 98 bis, as you know, this an Anglo-Saxon procedure, and the procedure is the following: It is the accused who takes the floor first to say that the Prosecutor has not provided any evidence for such and such a count, and you explain why. After that, the Prosecutor states his or her position. It is not the other way around. And I believe you thought that it was the other way round. It is first you who states your position. You will have one day to do so. And after that the Prosecutor will say why he or she believes that he or she has provided the evidence which will enable any trier of fact beyond all reasonable doubt on the basis of the evidence provided by the Prosecution to -- to enter a finding of guilt. That's how it goes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the only question is whether I will have the right to take the floor after the Prosecution again. That's what I'm most interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure you may since the Prosecutor always has the last word. As far as I'm concerned, it's not a problem. I have no problem with you taking the floor again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's what's most important for me. There are three things I would like to inform you of. Three problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today I received a decision from the Deputy Registrar, according to which my request for the financing of my defence is rejected. There are two versions of this decision. One is confidential and ex parte version. No question how this is possible, but the Registrar can do things that not a single legal system can do anywhere in the world, so it's no longer necessary to go into that, but I'm tired of making these requests now and of quibbling with the Registry. If the Tribunal refuses to finance my defence, then I won't present a defence case, and that will be the end of the matter. Secondly, and this is a far more important question for me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question. You don't wish to present your case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't present my defence case if it's not being financed. It hasn't been financed for seven and a half years. My associates can no longer continue working with me. It's difficult to co-operate with me, to work with me. It's easier for my enemies and my adversaries to work with me than for my associates because I exhaust people. First of all, I work a lot and then I burden everyone else around me with work. So it's very difficult to work with me. So why should they be tortured. They have done a lot of work. I haven't paid them a penny. The Registry says that my defence will not be financed, and, therefore, I will not present a defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, as far as this extremely delicate question is concerned, as I'm sure you understand, the Trial Chamber has always done all it could for you to be able to have associates that would be paid by the Tribunal. We have asked the Serbian authorities to provide us with any document which would enable us to assess your financial situation. The Serbian authorities have told us that the Registrar had all this information at their disposal. I must tell you that I was very surprised to discover that some documents, when I was a Pre-Trial Judge, had not been disclosed to me. That is another issue. As things stand today from a legal point of view, the Registrar has notified you and said that he would do no more than he has done so far, because in his view you do not meet the legal requirements which were to advise him of your exact situation. The Registrar has therefore sent the document which we have received, which is a document that presents itself as considering. It is up to you to see what resources you have to challenge the Registrar's position. You have a whole battery of resources available to you, and if need be, you may also seize the Trial Chamber. You have -- you may appeal. You may appeal this, and you may seize the Trial Chamber, and the Trial Chamber can rule on it. Beyond this issue of the funding of your case, we are there to act as custodians of the right to a fair trial. The statute is a legal standard that goes beyond directive or any administrative assessment. As Judges, we are bound to guarantee that the trial unfolds under fair conditions. So you have this possibility. You may seize the Trial Chamber to challenge this. You have just provided with us a new piece of information which is important. In other words, if you don't have the resources to present your case, you will waive that right. That is what I have understood, that you would not present your defence. In other words, you would waive that right because the Registrar will not provide you with the adequate resources. If I have not understood you correctly, please let me know. Based on that, in this particular situation the Trial Chamber must say something, because we are here to render justice. There is a Prosecutor that has issued an indictment. A judgement must be issued in light of this indictment. The international community made up of victims who are waiting for justice to be rendered, either to enter a finding of guilt, either -- or to acquit you. That will be based on the evidence provided. This is how things stand. The Registrar, to sum up, has handed down a decision. You may challenge this now, and things are now for you to react to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, according to the rules of the Tribunal, I could now file an appeal or complain to the President of the court -- of the Tribunal, but I won't do that. Recently I had a dental examination. That was at the beginning of the year. They X-rayed a certain number of teeth, quite a few of my teeth, as this hadn't been done for a long time. They noticed that at the root of a tooth that supports a bridge, they noticed that there was a bag or -- full of bacteria. I really don't really know what the term is. This tooth has to be taken out. A new bridge has to be constructed or an implant is needed. The doctor and the dentist have informed me of this. I complained to the President of the court. They asked him for a report. They told him I had gingivitis, and they said that they couldn't do that. Why I had gingivitis? Gingivitis means an inflammation around the teeth. When you have that, you can feel it. I don't feel anything. Gingivitis is an inflammation of the gums, and I am saying that I don't have such an inflammation, maybe if I had such and inflammation, even if I had gingivitis, they could do this intervention. Because in a few days' time, I might have a problem and I might not be able to appear at court. This root has to be taken out and has to be replaced with something. I don't want to come here with teeth missing. I need a dental implant or a new bridge. An implant is more -- a more modern technique. This costs a lot in the Netherlands. They don't want to do this. The President of the Tribunal responded to me on the basis of that report, but the report is based on erroneous information that was provided to the President. I'm waiting to see whether I'll have such an inflammation now. I don't want such an inflammation. I'm not trying to do anything to cause such an inflammation, but you know when you have these bacteria around a root, it's quite a problem. This is a time-bomb. Perhaps it suits certain people -- the fact that I'm in such a situation perhaps suits certain people. I said that I won't do anything about this financing. I told you about that a few years ago, but I'd also like to tell you that the Registry considers itself to be a body that is superior to me. They're superior to me or above me only in one respect. They can issue an order for security officers to escort me somewhere and to detain me in a unit, that's all. It's only in that sense that they're above me. Only in the sense of the constraints I'm subjected to. Most of the detainees are subjected to such constraints but not everyone. They have privileges. Some have privileges, but the Registry can't tell me what I have to do. This is what they have learnt in other cases. Sometimes if it suits them, they'll pay a lawyers immediately; if not, they won't pay them immediately. There are various ways in which you can manipulate lawyers. So I've concluded with that matter. There will be no financing of the Defence. There will be no Defence case. I'll move on to my second subject. Over ten days ago I arranged for a meeting for my main legal advisor. I only have one legal advisor, since you have of removed Zoran Krasic. Slavko Jerkovic has left me. Only Boris Aleksic remains. I had arranged a meeting with him and a meeting with a legal advisor for the other case for contempt of court. This was the lawyer Dejan Mirovic, and I also agreed on a meeting with the case manager in that other case, Nemanja Sarovic, a lawyer who is no longer acting as a lawyer but he has a lot of experience and knowledge. I still don't know when these meetings will take place. Boris Aleksic keeps phoning a representative of the Tribunal, a representative from OLAD. I haven't had a response. They're preventing such a meeting from taking place. They can't prevent me from meeting with my legal advisors. I have to meet with them. I have to agree on how to prepare requests pursuant to Rule 98 bis. I have to exchange documents with them, provide new documents to them. They have to return old documents to me. They have to give me the results of certain investigation teams, and so on and so forth. These meeting were to take place on the 15th and 16th of July. I asked for the trips to be paid. They have rejected this request. So they are awaiting for this hearing to be concluded so that I can't draw your attention to the problem and then they can do whatever they like until the end of August or the beginning of September. This meeting is essential for me. I have assigned them certain tasks for both cases that are concerned, and they have to brief me as to what they have done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please allow me to say something. I and my colleagues have noted all these problems. It is quite clear that if your associate Boris Aleksic does not assist you this may have consequences. That is fairly obvious. As you know, the Registrar, has the discretion vested in the statute and the rules, and the statute to me is the highest standard of law. The statute grants the Registrar the power to administer matters as well as management of resources and the budget of the Tribunal, but the Registrar does not have the discretion to interfere in a trial, and this is what I fear. In September now, given that time is running on, you may turn round and say that you cannot continue with this trial under those conditions. I shall stop everything. I am a responsible Judge. I have a lot of experience. I know that sometimes a cog in the wheel can derail a trial. This is what the situation looks like today and is a great subject of concern. This is something we have discussed among ourselves and we have done everything we could. I would like to draw your attention on the existence of a directive which has to do with the assignment of counsel. This is a French version of this directive, but I'm sure you will be able to handle that. In Article 13: Recourse against the decision taken by the Registrar. The accused who understands that the assignment of counsel has been rejected and this applies mutatis mutandis and who does not have sufficient funds to pay a lawyer can 15 days after the decision of the Registrar has been notified to him, which is the case since the Registrar has notified the letter to you, may file a motion before the Trial Chamber. He must appear before the Trial Chamber. May then, and listen carefully, either confirm the decision of the Registrar or cancel the Registrar's decision and decide that a counsel must be assigned or give instructions to the Registrar to reassess the situation and see whether the accused is in a position where he can pay a counsel. These are the conditions under which you can seize the Trial Chamber. We can cancel the decision of the Registry. We can assign a counsel. And the Registry clearly states that this applies to your situation. We can take a number of decisions if need be. I shall ask the usher to hand this to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I certainty won't give up everything that I can have recourse to, and I will certainly not give up the possibility of making a closing statement. I will prepare such a closing statement and present it here. As to whether I'll file a motion pursuant to Rule 98 bis or not, I don't know. I'll see. If next week the Registry prevents this meeting from taking place, well, we'll see how perfidious they are. They still haven't taken an official decision that I can contest. My legal advisor and case manager is supposed to travel on Wednesday, and they, and I know this on the basis of my experience, they are in a position to provide me with this decision on Sunday evening. They say they can come, but their visit has to be monitored. I don't want to have such a visit. Once I gave in and I regretted it. When they took me to some sort of gas chamber where our conversation was recorded. We didn't even manage to put up with it for the entire day. We could only put up with it for a few hours and then we left. If they violate this basic right of mine, the right to have my legal advisor and case manager visit me, if they prevent me from exchanging documents with them, assigning new tasks to them, if they prevent me from receiving reports from them as to what they have done, why should I file a motion pursuant to Rule 98 bis? I'll go directly to my closing statement in such a case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, on these issues, the Trial Chamber cannot step in. It is up to you to seize the President of this Tribunal. He can check on the Registry's actions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Lattanzi, if the Trial Chamber informs me next Wednesday that I can't have a meeting, my associates will be in The Hague on Wednesday, they will then go back on Thursday, because they won't be able to meet me. Then I can complain to the President of the Tribunal and if he approves of this meeting then my advisors will be here in August again. So this is a ping-pong game. I have gotten used to during these eight years here at The Hague Tribunal but that's not important. I said I would certainly give a closing statement in these proceedings. I have certain possibilities that I can avail myself of, or I can not avail myself of those possibilities and tell you why. Let's move on to a third subject which is the most important one for me. Perhaps it's not that important for you, but it's very important for me. A few days ago, one of the most wanted Serbian criminals and gangsters, Milos Simovic, was arrested by the Serbian police while he was trying to illegally cross the border between Croatia and Serbia. He sent a letter of some kind to the someone, to the Prosecution, a policeman, who knows to whom. This letter hasn't yet been disclosed. And allegedly, he said in that letter that I ordered the murder of Tomislav Nikolic from The Hague Tribunal. The Prosecution doesn't have to rise right now. It's an important matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I appreciate why this is an important matter for the accused but it is certainly not an administrative matter. It has been addressed in the press to the accused and his representative have addressed these issues in the press. And there is no reason for the Court to have to spend resources on this, and I'm looking around and I guess there's at least 15 or 20 people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there is a reason for the Trial Chamber to look into this. So go ahead, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to deal with this, because on the 2nd of July, "Blic" published a two-page article stating that The Hague Tribunal asked for information on Seselj's plan. The Judge Jean-Claude Antonetti is mentioned here, and it says that the letter was written to the Council for Co-operation with The Hague Tribunal. Apparently information was requested. So this directly relates to the work of the Chamber, and I have the right to say what I wanted to say. This criminal apparently said that I ordered the assassination of Tomislav Nikolic. You're well aware of the affair with Tomislav Nikolic. I don't have to repeat this. You probably remembered about two years ago Tomislav Nikolic also appeared in public with false claims, according to which I had ordered his assassination. That he mentioned certain unknown people from Republika Srpska. At the time everything had been calculated to make my position here in The Hague more difficult, to ensure that certain restrictive measures were taken against me and to spread some sort of propaganda in public, amongst the public. I immediately told my Defence team to investigate the whole matter. They found out that Aleksandar Vucic, Nikolic's deputy, my former legal advisor and the lawyer Zelimir Cabrilo and the lawyer Miodrag Rasic were both defending the criminal Miloslav Simovic and they had agreed to instruct the gangster Miloslav Simovic to make false charges against me; according to which I had ordered the assassination of Nikolic. They wanted to spread this propaganda in public so that support is provided for Tomislav Nikolic, whose party is disintegrating. They wanted to make it seem as if Seselj wanted to kill Tomislav Nikolic again. Three members of my Defence team, Vjerica Radeta, Nemanja Sarovic, Jelena Bozic, Talija [phoen], filed a criminal report against Aleksandar Vucic, Zelimir Cabrilo and Miodrag Rasic, and they requested that the relevant state authorities launch an investigates into the matter. I have a certified copy of this for you. Then after this affair started, after it gone blown out of all proportion in the media, Tomislav Nikolic appeared with the claim that I had already previously, three years ago, used Aleksandar Vucic, who, at the time, was my legal advisor, to order the assassination of someone. He didn't want to say who was concerned. Aleksandar Vucic said that perhaps he would say who it was, who was to be assassinated. The members of my Defence team also filed a criminal report against Tomislav Nikolic and insisted that the relevant state authorities clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, rather than going into details, go to the core of the matter. The Trial Chamber would not want -- does not want you to use this hearing to make political speeches, but I'll tell you later on why I stepped in and took the floor but go to the core of the matter immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the -- this isn't a political speech. I'm just speaking about legally relevant facts and criminal reports, and since you asked information from the Council for Co-operation with The Hague Tribunal in Serbia, I assume you want -- want to hear the other side and have an insight into the two criminal reports. Now, what is the greatest problem for me now is this: It's that Tomislav Nikolic and Aleksandar Vucic claim that through my wife, Jadranka Seselj, I ordered the killing of Tomislav Nikolic. I put out a contract to disqualify her and to have restrictive measures imposed upon me by The Hague Tribunal with respect to her future visits to me. She was once falsely accused in 2006 by the Prosecutor of having uttered the names of protected witnesses at a time when I was not disclosed any of the names of the protected witnesses by the Prosecution yet. And now I come to the crux of the matter. A man called Dejan Anastasijevic appears. He wasn't on the witness list at all, and he claims that The Hague Tribunal, several years ago, provided him with information whereby I had ordered his killing through my wife and that of some other people. Now, I wanted to tell you one thing. These are all lies and libel. Now accusations are being raised again that I was involved in Zoran Djindjic's, the Mafia prime minister's killing. I was never involved in any killing, never in my life or in any dishonourable criminal act. I was just charged for political crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The accused should formulate some sort of request or relief he is seeking from the Chamber. He has asked for nothing. He has spoken now for ten minutes and he we haven't heard what he wants --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I announced that it would last 20 minutes so we have enough time, as far as I can see, and I hope you will have the patience to hear me out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I must register my objection against this. I do not see how this, all of this, which may be disturbing to you, can possibly affect this trial. So I think we should --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] Well, Mr. Harhoff, your colleague Judge Antonetti can inform you of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let me step in immediately because do I not agree with what my fellow Judge, Judge Harhoff, just said. You said yourself that in 2006 already you had been subject to a number of problems, restrictions who led to problems, and I remember all the consequences you -- you were tapped. You could not have access to your privileged associates, and so on, and there was consequences on the trial. So when I read just like everybody else that in the press there was something about an assassination attempt, I immediately drew the connection between this and the possible consequences that we could have here in this trial. And I wrote to the ministry in charge of co-operation so that he would give me all necessary information on the investigates underway at the moment. What is important is investigates and not rumours or press clippings, and up until now I have not received any news from the ministry. The press seems to be challenging -- challenge you and saying that you are party to a number of assassination attempts, but my -- what I fear is that there might be consequences on this case, on this trial, and I believe that this is the direct connection. If there is evidence that could say or could prove or demonstrate that through your wife you have been able from yourself to order assassination attempts to be carried out, there will be -- there will be consequences, of course, but we need an investigates to know exactly what the facts are. I have full trust in the Serbian authorities and I'm sure that they will immediately or very soon tell us whether these rumours are founded or not, because the trial could be disturbed by this affair.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, that the dispatch that you sent to the Serbian authorities on this issue was sent in your name personally and not in the name of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Judge Harhoff is right. I believe that it was my duty to do so. I had offered -- I asked my fellow Judges whether they wanted to sign the letter with me, but they didn't -- they turned me down, so I believe that as the President of this Chamber, as person in charge of the administration of this -- of the smooth running of this trial I wanted to get to the source of the information, and it's only the Serbian authorities who can tell us whether these are rumours or whether there is any basis to this. But so far I haven't heard anything from the Serbian authorities. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, in these eight years I have had some very bad experience with the Hague Tribunal. At the end of 2003 and throughout the first half of 2004, all visits to me were banned as were all telephone conversations because my party had achieved significant results at the parliamentary elections and to prevent me having any influence and wielding any influence on the formation of the new Serbian government. In 2005, for two months, I had no visits, no telephone conversations. I wasn't even able to receive letters, even the letters that are checked anyway or any documents from my associates, because the Prosecution accused me of having disclosed the name of a protected witness, whereas I didn't even know that he could have been on the list of witnesses in my trial. In 2006, one the main reasons for my hunger strike was that at the initiative of the Prosecution, there were restriction with respect to my wife visiting me. Later on, the President of the Tribunal revoked that decision, but only after that had happened. Now I feel that there is this danger looming that -- whereby the Registry or the Prosecutor could apply the same measures, and that is why today I have supplied you with a list of all the medicines I take on a daily basis, and I want to tell you that if any restrictions are imposed with respect to my wife visiting me, then I will stop taking these medicaments. And you're free to consult any physicians and they'll tell you what that would mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please refrain from blackmail. The situation is very complex. I'm sure you understand this. Some restrictive measures can be placed upon you ordered by the Registrar, and then you can contest them and challenge them by seizing the President. That's what you should do. Now, what I'm worried about is the following: We are now finished with the first phase of this trial. A few weeks from now we will enter into Rule 98 bis. It's a short procedure, short stage of the procedure, and then it will be up to you to present your case, and this is possible, but everyone has to be fully aware of this. Now, I'm talking about everyone. I believe everyone understood who exactly is involved in this everyone. My fellow Judges and Judge Lattanzi, I agree with her and I'm sure Judge Harhoff also agrees with me, we were very impressed by the list of medicine that you have to take -- or you have an impressive list of medicine that you have to take. Of course there's medical confidentiality. You don't have to tell us why you have to take all these drugs, but you always said that you were very open. What are these drugs for? Maybe if you don't take them they'll jeopardise your health. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no secrets. Every doctor will be able to explain to you what those medicines are. I'm not an expert in the field. They're blood pressure pills, heart arrhythmia pills and pills against tachycardia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these are pills for your heart conditions, so it's very important. What you have said is now on the transcript. The Registrar will know about it, and he will see what he can decide as to your wife and your associates, whether they can visit you or not. As far as I'm concerned I must say that I see no reason why you shouldn't see your associates and your wife, as long as the investigation underway in Belgrade hasn't concluded that you actually took part in an offence. You have a presumption of innocence right now, and I don't think that we should draw any conclusions on what are rumours and only rumours at the moment. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at page 106, line 12 onward, 13, Your Honour has now said that we have now finished the first phase of this trial. I wish to put on record that the Prosecution is not in a position to close its case at this stage. I don't know whether that was what Your Honour intended to -- to indicate, that the Prosecution case is finished. There are a number of outstanding motions that are still pending that relate to evidentiary issues. Some are confidential, so I can't mention them in public session, and there are other reasons why I cannot mention some of them, but I believe there are 14 outstanding motions that need to be ruled on. There is one of them which is a request for leave to supplement the Prosecution's witness list to call two investigators. There's no decision on that yet. So if that motion is granted, we obviously still need to call witnesses or hear those witnesses. From that arise a particular issue because of the Trial Chamber's decision rendered on the 29th of June because of the status of those investigators who are now maybe the subject of investigations. So the position is unclear as to whether it would be possible to hear those witnesses if the Prosecution's request is granted. Moreover --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for you not to waste any time, Mr. Marcussen, you're absolutely right. There's still 14 pending motions, including one which is very important. It has to do with the Mladic diaries. And of course the Prosecution case will be closed only when we have rendered our decision on these 14 motions. Now, on regarding this special request, this special motion saying that you wanted to hear two investigators on possible allegations of intimidation on Prosecution cases switched to being so-called Defence witnesses. Since as you sold we did render a decision on June 29, 2010, asking the Registrar to appoint an amicus curiae. It's up to the Registrar to do this now. This is my position. It's not up to us. It's up to the Registrar. It's up to amicus curiae to hear these witnesses. This is my position, but the Trial Chamber has not ruled on this yet. Because it is the amicus curiae who will be competent to tell us whether there is sufficient grounds, because we're at the very early phase of the procedure. It's up to the amicus curiae to see whether there are sufficient grounds to do this. So regarding these two witnesses, I believe that it's important, but it's up to the amicus curiae to rule on this. I'm not competent, as far as this is concerned, given what was written in this June 29 decision, saying that it's up to the amicus curiae to tell the Trial Chamber whether there is sufficient grounds to draw an indictment. On the -- on the other hand we will rule on the other 13 pending motions. They're not overly technical except for the motion on the Mladic diaries, but we're waiting for your submissions on these ones, written submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to add that as far as some of these motions is concerned, we are still waiting for them to be translated, we're waiting for them to be translated into B/C/S and we're waiting for the answers by -- the reply by the accused. So this is why we can't rule on them yet, because the translation isn't done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to finish off, this is why I said that Rule 98 bis can only start as of September. This phase, the Rule 98 bis, can only start in September because this is going to be a lengthy process to get us there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, if the Prosecutor continues that way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give you the floor but I don't know yet what Mr. Seselj had to say. What did you have to say, Mr. Seselj or should I give the floor to Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Prosecutor continues that way, this could last another ten years. Judges, the Prosecutor has said everything he wanted to say during this case, and as far as his investigators are concerned, that is a matter of other proceedings. They can be interviewed and examined there, not here, because this trial is not against the Prosecutor here or against me for contempt of court for that matter so that their investigators can present things that might be significant here. All the evidence has been presented here in court, primary evidence as testimony viva voce, and original source documents if they were attached. Everything else is secondary evidence. And if the Prosecutor thinks that presenting two of his investigators that he's going to improve his very poor prosecuting positions here, it would be better if he were to admit a fiasco straight away. The Hague Tribunal, during this trial, has experienced a fiasco. You can, of course, sentence me to a hundred years' imprisonment but in the transcript of this trial and these proceedings you don't have the grounds to sentence me for even one year, and it's high time that the Prosecutor realises that. Do you want to start the trial all over again? Let him find another hundred witnesses. He can change the locations of the alleged crimes, perhaps he can accuse me of killing Kennedy or the civil war in Biafra or thins like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, you had the floor. You have it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought to detect that Judge Harhoff maybe was trying to intervene. It seemed he had something to say. I don't know if I should go first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, go ahead. We have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the evidence of the witness today reflect in the Prosecution's submission the very campaign of intimidation, interference that we have raised throughout the case. This witness is like other witnesses, in our submission, clearly fabricated evidence and lied to this Court. The Prosecution want to put on record that we have the right to seek to confront this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Prosecution please slow down for the sake of the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I am speaking, and I would like to finish what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let Mr. Marcussen finish what he has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There have been other witnesses. They have in our submission clearly fabricated evidence and lied to this Court. The Prosecution want to put on record that it has the right to seek to confront these fabrications of evidence. The allegations against OTP investigators, especially Ms. Pradham, is completely unfounded and the Prosecution wishes to confront this and consider calling further evidence. We want to make clear on the record that we reject the false allegations and the fabricated evidence of the last witness, and unless the Court indicates that it is not necessary because the witness evidence is blatantly false, we wish to call evidence immediately if necessary to confront it. And, Your Honours, these kind of allegations have been made by a number of witnesses throughout the case and notably since the trial restarted in January and a number of court witnesses were called. The Chamber questioned these witnesses about the way their statements were taken. The Trial Chamber's decision from the 29th of June is going to lead to the -- has opened up the question of the reliability of statements that the Trial Chamber has already admitted into evidence, and it may, indeed, be necessary for the Prosecution also to call evidence with respect to allegations made by other witnesses, because now what has happened with the decision from the 29th of June seem to be that a whole range of allegations have been in our submissions reopened subsequent to -- subsequent to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, let me stop you. You're an excellent trial attorney, one of the best senior trial attorneys we have here. You know that this decision -- well, we have been seized of a motion for contempt of court against three eminent members of the OTP. What are we supposed to do, throw it out? This is not what I think justice -- what I think of justice. The Trial Chamber, who was presided by President Robinson, Judge Bonomy and myself did say that this motion would be dealt with during the trial. It's not me who said this. It's the President of this Tribunal. And that at the end of the trial we would rule on this in light of the new elements that are spelled out in the June 29 decision. We did say that we need to have an amicus curiae to look into this now, which does not mean that we -- of course, we don't necessarily believe what the witnesses said, but the amicus curiae will be there to check the evidence. That's the truth. So please don't say what you said, because this goes against the decision of June 29, 2010. You asked for certification of appeal. Fine. We'll see how things turn out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, you also, yourself, presented and the accused used it in open session, you presented a statement made by an interpreter. You don't only have evidence provided by witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and to add something because I wanted to put my own opinion in this decision. The interpreter clearly stated how the whole -- how everything occurred. It's up to the amicus curiae to look into this. We can no longer take -- rule on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, we need to finish now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was not intending at all to go into the merit of the 29 June decision. My point was that it raises a number of issues which mean that we cannot -- the Prosecution cannot close its case. That was the submission I was making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, 15 seconds, because we must leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, with the speed of lightning. Judges, you should have intervened, in my opinion, when Mr. Marcussen called today's witness a false witness or, rather, when he claimed that the witness had given false testimony. Now, intentionally during the cross-examination I didn't want to deal with any pre-history when the ping-pong ball was going, when the ball was in my court, then in the Prosecutor's court and then back to me. I adhered to the Muslim sources, Muslim document sources. I looked through them and you were able to see on that basis than -- that the statement he gave to the Prosecutor was not truthful. Now, the fact that the Prosecutor at the beginning rallied a large number of witnesses and promising them third country sojourn and apartments and fulfilled those promises to only some of them, but not to most of them, and when the witnesses were disillusioned they started scattering. You know when people live poorly, in poverty, some people are ready to give false testimony, not everyone, but some are. Now do you remember that witness whom the witness gave up on later on who bartered with the Prosecution as to how he was going to testify before he came into court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have mentioned the Trial Chamber will hand down its decision and we will certainly meet again in September.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
